topics.title: Abiding in God
topics.summary: Dwelling in God's presence is the foundation of life. God is life and light, and everything in all creation testifies to him. To abide in Him is to remain rooted in His love, drawing strength and purpose from an unbroken connection with the only one who truly saves.

topics.title: Access to God
topics.summary: Through Christ, every believer in him has bold and confident access to the Father. No barrier of sin or status can prevent the redeemed from approaching God's throne of grace and mercy.

topics.title: Adultery & Infidelity
topics.summary: Scripture warns strongly against unfaithfulness in marriage, treating it as a violation of sacred covenant. God calls His people to purity and honor in all intimate relationships, and often times the fruit we produce in these relationships are a reflection of our love for Christ. It can be helpful to hold our relationship with Christ side-by-side the relationship(s) we have here on earth to see where our heart truly is.

topics.title: Affections & Passions
topics.summary: Where we set our affections shapes who we become. God invites us to direct our deepest passions toward things above and not on earth– letting a holy desire that comes from him, transform our everyday pursuits by the renewing of our mind.

topics.title: Afflictions
topics.summary: Suffering is not only meant to make you feel the sorrow. It has purpose for you. It will strengthen you. It will build character in you. It will teach you lessons that you wouldn't have learned by having it the easy way. It will give you a testimony and point you towards the one who is really your true strength– Jesus. Scripture reveals numerous times that afflictions refine faith, produce endurance, and draw the heart closer to God who comforts all who mourn. Take heart in this season, knowing that it shall pass, and delight in him, knowing that he is the one who will bring it to a close in its due time.

topics.title: Agriculture & Farming
topics.summary: From Eden forward, land has been central to God's provision. The biblical principles of sowing, reaping, and stewardship for example, mirror spiritual life and God's faithfulness... We're called to not become tired or build expectations for immediate results. There's a season, a place, and a time for everything.

topics.title: Altars
topics.summary: Altars in Scripture are places of sacrifice, worship, and encounter with God. They mark moments of surrender and memorial to God's faithfulness, and are also places of reverence.

topics.title: Angels
topics.summary: Angels are God's mighty servants. They're sent to minister to believers. They deliver messages to us on earth. And they often times reveal, or carry out divine judgments. Angels show us the grandeur of heaven's order.

topics.title: Anger
topics.summary: While righteous anger has its place, unchecked wrath destroys relationships and grieves the Spirit. Scripture calls believers to be slow to anger and quick to forgive; putting off all things that hinder you from walking well yoked to Christ.

topics.title: Antichrist
topics.summary: Scripture warns of coming deceivers who oppose Christ and exalts themselves(himself) above all that is worshiped. Believers are called to discernment in the last day– to test the spirits, and to be watchful.

topics.title: Apostles
topics.summary: The apostles were ordinary men called by Jesus, given power, and sent out as His witnesses to the very ends of the earth. On their teaching, with Christ Himself as the cornerstone, the church still stands. The earliest believers devoted themselves to that doctrine, to fellowship, to breaking bread, and to prayer — and we're invited to build our lives on nothing less.

topics.title: Army & Armed Forces
topics.summary: Scripture honors the soldier's calling — courage, discipline, endurance — and points it toward a greater battle. Our true fight isn't with flesh and blood, which is why God supplies His own armor for standing firm against the enemy's schemes. Serve with integrity and contentment, refuse the entanglements that dull a good soldier, and take heart: the Lord goes with you wherever you are sent.

topics.title: Asking & Receiving
topics.summary: God is a Father who loves to be asked. Jesus tells us plainly to ask, to seek, to knock — and promises an open door to the one who does. Yet how we ask matters; petitions aimed at feeding our own lusts go unanswered, while requests shaped by His will are surely heard. Bring your desires boldly to Him in Jesus' name, and pray believing.

topics.title: Baptism
topics.summary: Baptism is a burial and a resurrection. Going under the water, we identify with Christ in His death; coming up, we rise to walk in new life, clothed in Him. It is a good conscience giving its answer to God, joined to repentance and the promised gift of His Spirit — and it is the pattern Jesus sent His church to carry to every nation.

topics.title: Blasphemy
topics.summary: The name of the Lord is holy, and Scripture never treats it lightly. To speak against God, to drag His name through the mud, or to use it emptily is no small thing — He will not count the careless guiltless. Jesus even warns of one blasphemy that carries no forgiveness: hardened, willful slander against the Holy Spirit. Guard the worthy name you are called by; let your lips honor it.

topics.title: Blood
topics.summary: Life itself is carried in the blood — which is why God appointed it, from the earliest altars, to make atonement for the soul. Every old-covenant sacrifice pointed ahead to a better one: Jesus, who loved us and washed away our sins at the cost of His own life. Through His blood we have redemption and forgiveness, and as we walk in His light, it keeps on cleansing us from every sin.

topics.title:
Character of
Saints
topics.summary: A saint's character isn't manufactured — it's grown. The Spirit bears His fruit in surrendered lives: love, joy, peace, patience, gentleness, and the rest. So clothe yourself daily in mercy, humility, and forgiveness; let love be genuine, hate what is evil, hold tight to what is good. You were called out of darkness for this very purpose — that your life would put His praises on display.

topics.title: Christ is God
topics.summary: Jesus is not merely a great teacher — He is God. He was present in the beginning as the Word, and nothing exists that He did not make. All the fullness of deity dwells in Him bodily; He and the Father are one; the Father Himself addresses the Son as God, enthroned forever and ever. Who you say He is changes everything.

topics.title:
Character of
Christ
topics.summary: Look closely at Jesus and you see both what God is like and what we are meant to become. Though equal with God, He took the posture of a servant — kneeling to wash the feet of His own disciples. Tempted at every point yet without a single sin, reviled yet refusing to revile back, He endured the cross for the joy set ahead of Him. His steps are our pattern; walk in them.

topics.title: Deliverance
topics.summary: The righteous cry out, and the Lord hears — and He does more than hear; He delivers. He has rescued before, He is rescuing now, and He will rescue again. Near to the brokenhearted, a rock and a high tower for the pressed-down, He has already carried us out of darkness and into His dear Son's kingdom. Whatever surrounds you today, call on Him. Deliverance belongs to your God.

topics.title: Faith
topics.summary: Faith takes hold of what the eye cannot yet see. It comes alive as we hear God's word, it pleases Him like nothing else can, and it refuses to sit idle — belief with no works to show for it is dead. So walk by it, not by sight. Trust that God is, and that He rewards everyone who diligently seeks Him, and let your believing turn into doing.

topics.title: Fear
topics.summary: There is a fear that starts wisdom — reverence before the Lord — and a fear that torments. God never gave you the second kind. His Spirit carries power, love, and a sound mind; His presence walks the darkest valley with you; His perfect love drives fear out the door. When dread rises, remember whose right hand is upholding you.

topics.title: Forgiveness of Sins
topics.summary: No stain runs too deep for the mercy of God. Confess your sin, and He is faithful to forgive and to wash you fully clean — scarlet made white as wool and snow. He removes our transgressions farther than east is from west, blotting them out so seasons of refreshing can come from His presence. Don't keep carrying what He has already buried.

topics.title: Forgetfulness
topics.summary: Forgetting God rarely happens all at once. Often times it creeps in slowly — when we've eaten and are satisfied, when the houses are built and life is good — the very seasons Israel forgot His wonders and the hand that delivered them. That's why the Lord weaves remembrance into our walk: bread broken in memory of Him, warnings repeated, stories retold. Keep rehearsing what He has done, especially when things are going well.

topics.title: Giving to the Poor
topics.summary: When you give to the poor, you are lending to the Lord Himself — and He repays. Jesus goes further still: feed the hungry, clothe the naked, visit the sick and the prisoner, and you have done it unto Him. So give freely, not grudgingly or under pressure, for God loves the giver whose heart is glad. What you pour out returns to you in generous measure, pressed down and spilling over.

topics.title: God's Plans
topics.summary: God's intentions toward His children are good, even when the road makes no sense to us. His ways sit far above ours, and His counsel outlasts every generation. We may chart our own course, but it is the Lord who orders each step. Rest in this: nothing in your life falls outside His purpose, and for those who love Him, He is weaving it all toward good. Trust the Planner more than the plan you can see.

topics.title: Gossip
topics.summary: Often times the smallest whisper does the deepest damage. A gossiping tongue sows discord and separates even the closest of friends, and spreading what was shared in confidence marks an unfaithful spirit — love knows how to keep a matter covered. Our words are meant to build up and give grace to those who hear them. If we claim to follow Christ yet never bridle our tongue, we deceive our own hearts. Guard your mouth; it tells the truth about your heart.

topics.title: Grace
topics.summary: Grace is the gift none of us could ever earn. Salvation comes not by our striving but by what God freely gives, so no one has room to boast. And grace doesn't stop at saving us — it is strength in our weakness, and it teaches us to turn from ungodliness and live upright in this present age. Where sin ran deep, grace ran deeper still. From His fullness we keep receiving, gift upon gift.

topics.title: Healing
topics.summary: The Lord is a healer — of bodies and of souls. By the wounds Christ bore we are made whole, and the same Jesus who walked through Galilee restoring the sick still hears faith-filled prayer today. Call for the elders. Ask to be anointed and prayed over. Bring your sickness honestly before God, for He is the one who pardons every sin and touches every disease. When He heals you, you are healed indeed.

topics.title: Help in Troubles
topics.summary: When trouble comes, you do not face it alone. God is a refuge, a stronghold near at hand in the worst of days — even if mountains gave way and seas roared, He would still stand. Lift your eyes; your help comes from the Maker of all things, and He knows those who put their trust in Him. He takes hold of your hand and tells you not to fear. With the Lord as our helper, we can face whatever man or trial brings.

topics.title: Holiness
topics.summary: Holiness is not reserved for a select few — it is the calling of every believer, because the God who called us is holy Himself. Scripture even ties holiness to seeing the Lord, so we cannot treat it casually. Set yourself apart. Cleanse what defiles, in body and in spirit. Offer your whole life as a living offering, acceptable to God, and remember that He is the one doing the sanctifying work in you. Pursue peace with everyone, and pursue holiness with everything.

topics.title: Holy Spirit
topics.summary: The Holy Spirit is God's own presence dwelling in the believer. He is the Comforter Jesus promised — teaching us, reminding us of all Christ said, and leading us into truth. He gives power to witness, from our own streets to the farthest ends of the earth. And when we do not know how to pray, He intercedes for us with groanings deeper than words. Your body is now His temple; you no longer belong to yourself. Walk closely with Him.

topics.title: Love
topics.summary: Love sits at the center of who God is — and of who His children are becoming. Real love is patient. It is kind. It keeps no record of wrongs and never demands its own way. Jesus made love the mark of discipleship: the world will know we are His by the way we care for one another. There is no greater love than laying your life down for a friend, and that is exactly what Christ did for us. To love well is to fulfill the whole law.

topics.title: Lustfulness
topics.summary: Lust promises pleasure but delivers bondage. Jesus taught that sin begins in the heart long before it reaches the hands, and James traces the path plainly — desire entices, sin is conceived, and sin fully grown brings death. Cravings of the flesh and of the eyes are not from the Father; they wage war on your soul. So don't negotiate with them. Run. And as you flee, chase righteousness, faith, love, and peace alongside others who seek the Lord from a pure heart.

topics.title: Lying
topics.summary: Truth matters deeply to God — a deceitful tongue sits on the short list of things He hates. Lying belongs to the old self we put off when we came to Christ, and Jesus named the devil as the source of every lie; deception is his native language, not ours. We are members of one body, so speak honestly with one another. Those who deal truthfully are the Lord's delight, and He Himself is the Truth we now walk in.

topics.title: Marriage
topics.summary: Marriage was God's idea from the very beginning — two lives leaving the old behind and being joined as one flesh. It is a covenant He Himself ties, and what He has bound together no one should tear apart. Husbands are called to sacrificial love, patterned after the way Christ gave Himself up for His Church. Scripture calls the marriage bed honorable and worth guarding, and a godly spouse evidence of the Lord's favor. Hold your covenant in reverence; it preaches Christ to a watching world.

topics.title: Miracles
topics.summary: Our God still moves in power. The same Lord who split the sea for Israel walked among us in Jesus, whose wonders bore witness that God was truly with Him. And the works didn't end at the cross — Jesus promised that those who believe would carry His mission forward, with signs following as the gospel goes out. Miracles are never for show. They point past themselves, turning our eyes to the God who performs them as He wills and in His timing.

topics.title: Money
topics.summary: Money makes a useful servant and a cruel master. Jesus was plain about it — no heart can serve both God and wealth. It is not money itself but the love of it that has pierced so many with sorrow and pulled them away from the faith. Work honestly, for riches gained by empty means dwindle while steady labor grows. Be content with what you have; the God who promises never to abandon you is worth more than any balance. Prove faithful in the little things, and He will trust you with true riches.

topics.title: Old Ways
topics.summary: In Christ, you are not who you used to be. The old self — with its darkened thinking, its habits, its deeds — was crucified with Jesus so that sin would no longer rule over you. Whoever belongs to Christ is a new creation entirely; the former things have gone and everything has become new... So stop reaching back for what already died. Put on the new self, renewed in the knowledge of your Creator, and let the life you live now be lived by faith in the Son who loved you and gave Himself up for you.

topics.title: Preaching & Teaching
topics.summary: God has chosen to save the world through the telling of good news — what looks like foolishness to men is His power to rescue those who believe. How can anyone call on a Savior they have never heard of? Someone must go, and someone must speak. So make disciples of the nations, teach what Christ commanded, and know He goes with you to the end of the age. Stay ready in convenient seasons and inconvenient ones alike, handling God's word with the care of a workman who has nothing to be ashamed of.

topics.title: Salvation
topics.summary: Salvation is God's gift from beginning to end. He loved the world enough to give His only Son, not to condemn us but to rescue us. It cannot be earned by works or bought with our own goodness; it comes by grace, through faith, according to His mercy and the washing of renewal. There is no other name that can save us. Confess Jesus as Lord, believe in your heart that God raised Him, and you will be saved.

topics.title: Satan & the Devil
topics.summary: The devil is real, and he is not idle. Scripture calls him our adversary, prowling like a lion looking for someone to devour, a liar and a murderer from the start. But he is a defeated enemy. Submit yourself to God, resist him, and he must flee. Remember that our battle is not against people; it is against spiritual powers of darkness, and victory belongs to those covered by the Lamb's blood and the testimony on their lips.

topics.title: Sickness
topics.summary: God does not abandon the sick. The Lord sustains His children on the bed of illness, and when Jesus walked the cities and villages, He healed every kind of sickness and disease. If you are sick, call on the church to pray; the prayer offered in faith carries real power, and the Lord is the one who raises up. Hold on to the promise ahead, when He wipes every tear away and pain itself is no more.

topics.title: Sin
topics.summary: Every one of us has sinned and fallen short of God's glory. Sin is the breaking of God's law, and it never stays small: desire conceives it, and when it is full grown it brings forth death. To claim we have none is to deceive ourselves. But when we confess, God is faithful to forgive and to cleanse us from every stain. Sin's wages are death— the gift God offers instead is eternal life in Jesus Christ.

topics.title: Temptation & Trials
topics.summary: No temptation you face is unique to you, and none is beyond what you can bear; God is faithful, and He always makes a way out. So watch and pray, because the flesh grows weak even when the spirit is willing. When trials come, don't waste them. The testing of your faith works patience in you, and that faith is more precious to Him than gold that fades. Jesus knows what it is to be tempted— and he is able to help you through it.

topics.title: The Great Tribulation
topics.summary: Scripture speaks plainly of a coming time of trouble unlike anything the world has ever known. Yet even there, God's mercy governs. Those days are shortened for the sake of His elect, and He promises to keep those who hold fast to His word through the hour that will test all the earth. The sun will darken, the heavens will shake, but the story ends with Christ appearing in power and glory. Take heart. The Lamb's blood washes robes white, and His people come through.

topics.title: Wealth & Riches
topics.summary: Money makes a terrible master. Whoever loves silver is never satisfied by it, and the one who trusts in riches will fall, while the righteous flourish like a branch. Scripture points us higher: store up treasure in heaven, where nothing rusts and no thief can reach, for where your treasure sits, your heart settles too. If God has given you much, hold it loosely... trust the living God who supplies richly, and be wealthy in good works instead.

topics.title: Wives
topics.summary: A virtuous wife is worth far more than rubies. Her husband's heart safely rests in her, and her life does him good all her days. Scripture calls wives to honor their husbands as they would the Lord, mirroring the way the church follows Christ, and it prizes a beauty that isn't outward at all: a gentle and quiet spirit, the kind that can win a husband over without a single word. Whoever finds a wife has found a good thing, and favor from the Lord with it.

topics.title: Wisdom
topics.summary: Get wisdom, Scripture says: it is the principal pursuit, and with it, get understanding. Reverence for the Lord is where it begins, every treasure of it lies hidden in Christ, and unlike money, wisdom gives life to those who hold it. If you lack it, just ask. God gives generously to everyone who comes, and He will never scold you for asking.

topics.title: Knowledge of God
topics.summary: Knowing God is not a bonus for the extra spiritual; it is eternal life itself. He desires it more than sacrifice and burnt offerings, and everything we need for life and godliness flows out of it. Paul counted all he had as loss, rubbish even, next to the surpassing worth of knowing Christ Jesus his Lord. Press in to know Him, and grace and peace will be multiplied to you along the way.

topics.title: Discernment
topics.summary: Discernment grows with use. Like muscles trained by exercise, our senses learn to separate good from evil as we mature on the solid food of the word. Don't believe every spirit; test them, because many false voices are loose in the world. Ask God for an understanding heart the way Solomon did, and pray your love would keep growing in knowledge and depth of judgment, so you can approve what is excellent until the day Christ appears.

topics.title: Fear of the Lord
topics.summary: To fear the Lord is not to cower before Him; it is awe, reverence for who God actually is. Scripture calls it the starting point of both knowledge and wisdom, a wellspring of life that steers us clear of death's traps. Paired with humility, it leads to riches, honor, and life that lasts. When Solomon weighed everything under the sun, his conclusion was simple: fear God and walk in His commands, for this is the whole of what we were made for.

topics.title: Humility
topics.summary: Lowliness is the posture heaven honors. God stands against the proud, but the humble receive His grace, so clothe yourself in humility and count others as more important than yourself. Micah says it plainly: do justly, love mercy, walk humbly with your God. Bring yourself low before the Lord, and He himself will be the one to lift you up.

topics.title: Pride
topics.summary: Pride walks ahead of destruction, and a haughty spirit ahead of a fall. It promises to lift us up, yet Scripture says it brings shame and drags a man low, while honor upholds the humble. Worst of all, pride sets us opposite God himself, for He resists the proud and pours grace on the humble. Examine your heart honestly. In God's kingdom, the way up has always been down.

topics.title: Worship
topics.summary: True worship is what the Father is seeking: those who will worship Him in spirit and truth. Come, kneel before your Maker. Give the Lord the glory His name deserves, for He made all things, and they exist for His pleasure. We are receiving a kingdom that cannot be shaken, so let us serve Him acceptably, with reverence and awe, in the beauty of His holiness.

topics.title: Praise
topics.summary: Praise is the language of a heart that knows its God. Scripture invites us to come into His presence with thankful lips, to bless His name in every season— not only when life feels good. It's a sacrifice we offer continually, and everything that breathes was made to give it. Let praise fill your mouth today; He is worthy of it all.

topics.title: Thanksgiving
topics.summary: Gratitude is God's will for His people— not just when life goes well, but in every circumstance. When we bring our requests to Him with thankful hearts, worry loses its grip and His peace takes its place. Thanksgiving reminds the soul who its Provider is: the Lord who is good, whose mercy never runs out.

topics.title: Sabbath
topics.summary: Rest is not laziness— it's obedience. From the very beginning God set apart a day and blessed it, showing us we were never designed to run without stopping. The sabbath was given as a gift, not a burden, and a deeper rest still remains for God's people... In Christ we cease striving and trust His finished work. Call it a delight, and honor Him in it.

topics.title: Singing to the Lord
topics.summary: The Lord has done wonders, and a new song is the fitting response. Singing isn't reserved for the gifted— it rises from a heart where Christ's word has made its home. Whether with instruments or a quiet melody within, we tell of His salvation day after day. So sing. He holds the victory, and praise sits well on the lips of His people.

topics.title: Reverence
topics.summary: Our God is holy, and He is not to be approached carelessly. Scripture teaches us to guard our steps in His house— quicker to listen than to speak, remembering the fire of His holiness. Reverence isn't distance from God; it's honoring Him the way a son honors a good father. Serve Him with awe, and let your worship carry the weight His name deserves.

topics.title: Prayer
topics.summary: Nothing in your life is too small to bring to God. He invites us to pray about everything— our worries, our needs, our confessions, our thanks— and Jesus Himself gave us the pattern to follow. Scripture says a righteous heart's earnest prayer carries real power. So keep the conversation going. Pray in every season. Don't stop.

topics.title: Intercession
topics.summary: Standing in the gap for others is holy work. We're called to pray for all people— leaders, saints, strangers— and often times we don't even know what to say. That's where the Spirit steps in, carrying our prayers deeper than words can reach. Best of all, Christ ever lives to intercede for you. When you pray for others, you're joining a work heaven never stops doing.

topics.title: Fasting
topics.summary: When Jesus taught on fasting, His first warning was against doing it for an audience. Fasting is a quiet turning of the whole heart back to God— setting aside even good things to seek Him first. And the fast God chooses reaches outward too: loosing heavy burdens and freeing the oppressed. Jesus fasted. The early church fasted before big decisions. There is power in hungering for God more than bread.

topics.title: Watchfulness
topics.summary: You don't know the hour, so stay awake. Jesus told His disciples to watch and pray so temptation wouldn't catch them sleeping— our spirit may be willing, but our flesh tires easily. Scripture calls us to a sober, prayerful alertness that refuses to drift off while the end draws near. Live ready. The One you're waiting for could come at any moment.

topics.title: Persistence in Prayer
topics.summary: Jesus told a story about a widow who wouldn't quit— and He told it so we would pray and never lose heart. Ask. Seek. Knock. The promise is that everyone who keeps coming will receive, will find, will see the door opened. Delay is not denial. Continue steadfast in prayer with thanksgiving, patient in the waiting, trusting His timing over your own.

topics.title: Communion with God
topics.summary: God doesn't want visitors; He wants dwellers. Jesus promised that where love and obedience live, He and the Father come and make their home. Come close to Him, and He comes close to you— that's not poetry, it's a promise. There is a nearness reserved for those who revere Him, a fellowship with the Father and the Son that you were called into by God Himself.

topics.title: Hope
topics.summary: Because Jesus walked out of the grave, hope is alive— not wishful thinking, but an anchor for the soul, sure and steady in any storm. His mercies arrive fresh every morning; His compassion never fails. What we're waiting for we can't yet see, and that's exactly why we wait with patience. Let the God of all hope flood you with joy and peace as you believe.

topics.title: Joy
topics.summary: Joy runs deeper than happiness. It is the strength of God's people, and it doesn't hinge on circumstances— fullness of it is found in His presence. Jesus spoke so that His own joy would remain in us and make ours complete. That's how Scripture can tell us to rejoice always, even counting trials as an occasion for joy. Your gladness is anchored in a Person, not a season.

topics.title: Peace
topics.summary: The peace Jesus gives is nothing like the world's version— it doesn't depend on calm circumstances. Through faith we stand reconciled to God, and when we bring our anxieties to Him in prayer, a peace beyond understanding guards our hearts and minds. Keep your thoughts fixed on Him; He holds steady the one who trusts Him, and His peace can rule where worry once did.

topics.title: Comfort
topics.summary: God is not distant from your sorrow— He is a Father rich in mercy, the source of all true comfort. Even in the deepest valley He walks beside you, and His presence itself is the consolation. But comfort isn't meant to stop with you: He strengthens us in trouble so we can steady others walking the same road. If you mourn today, take heart— the Comforter Himself abides with you.

topics.title: Rest
topics.summary: True rest is found in a person, not a pause. Jesus invites the weary and burdened to come to him, take his easy yoke, and learn from his gentle and lowly heart. Like a shepherd, God leads us beside quiet waters and restores what the world wears down. Stop striving to carry it all yourself. His presence goes with you, and your soul can wait quietly on him — the rest he gives reaches all the way down.

topics.title: Patience
topics.summary: God does some of his deepest work in the waiting. Like the farmer who holds on through rain after rain for a harvest he cannot rush, we're called to stay steady until the promise arrives. Tribulation produces patience in us, and patience grows into proven character and hope. So don't grow weary in doing good. Due season is coming, and the Lord is good to the soul that quietly waits on him.

topics.title: The Gospel
topics.summary: The gospel is not advice — it is power. Christ died, was buried, and rose again, and everyone who believes this word of truth is saved and sealed with the promised Holy Spirit. Scripture warns us not to trade it for a counterfeit; there is no other good news that can save. Never be ashamed of it. Carry it to every creature in every corner of the world, because it remains God's own power to rescue all who believe.

topics.title: Witnessing
topics.summary: You don't need a stage to be a witness — you need a story and the Spirit. When Jesus healed a man, he simply sent him home to tell his friends all the Lord had done for him. That's where it starts. The Holy Spirit gives us power to speak, from our own city to the farthest parts of the earth, and we're called to be ready with a gentle answer for anyone who asks about the hope in us. What you have seen God do is worth telling.

topics.title: Discipleship
topics.summary: Following Jesus is a daily decision, not a one-time prayer. He calls us to deny ourselves, pick up our cross each morning, and come after him. Disciples continue in his word, and there the truth makes us free. Discipleship also multiplies — we're sent to teach the nations all he commanded, with his promise to be with us to the end. Bear much fruit. That's how the Father is glorified, and how the world knows whose we are.

topics.title: Repentance
topics.summary: To repent is to turn around and come home. Often times we confuse regret with repentance, but worldly sorrow works death, while godly sorrow turns us toward life and leaves nothing to regret. God now calls all people everywhere to turn from sin, and he is patient with us because he wants no one to perish. Turn to him, and your sins are blotted out. Times of refreshing follow the turning.

topics.title: The Church
topics.summary: Jesus is building his church, and the gates of hell will not overcome it. The church is less a building than a body — many members, one Spirit, every believer joined to Christ and to one another. He loved her enough to give himself up for her, to wash and sanctify her. The first believers devoted themselves to doctrine, fellowship, breaking bread, and prayer, and we're called to keep gathering too, stirring one another toward love and good works. Don't walk this out alone.

topics.title: Evangelism
topics.summary: The harvest is still plentiful, and the laborers are still few. How can people call on someone they haven't believed in, and how can they believe in someone they've never heard of? Somebody has to go. Somebody has to speak. When persecution scattered the early church, they preached the word everywhere they landed — sharing Christ wasn't a program, it was a way of life... Pray for laborers, and then be willing to become the answer to your own prayer.

topics.title: Trusting God
topics.summary: Our understanding will run out. God's faithfulness will not. Scripture calls us to trust the Lord wholeheartedly instead of leaning on our own reasoning, acknowledging him in every path we take. The one who trusts is like a tree set beside the water, still green when the heat arrives. So when fear shows up, make trust your reflex — what can flesh do to the child God keeps? He guards in perfect peace the mind that stays fixed on him.

topics.title: Seeking God
topics.summary: God rewards the seeker. His promise is plain: search for him with your whole heart, and you will find him. David went after him early, thirsting for God the way a dry land aches for water. Make the kingdom your first pursuit — before the worries, before the lists — and watch him add what you need. Then keep on seeking. His strength and his face are worth pursuing continually.

topics.title: Obedience
topics.summary: Obedience is love with its sleeves rolled up. Jesus put it plainly: loving him means keeping his commandments — not to earn grace, but in response to it. God delights in a listening heart more than in grand religious gestures; to obey means more to him than sacrifice ever did. So don't be a hearer only, quietly deceiving yourself. Do the word. Blessing rests on the one who hears what God says and actually keeps it.

topics.title: God's Presence
topics.summary: There is nowhere you can go that God is not already there. Heaven, the depths, the far side of the sea — even there his hand holds you. Joy finds its fullness in his presence, and his promise has never changed: his presence goes with his people, and rest comes with it. So fear not, and don't be dismayed; he strengthens, he helps, he upholds. The same Jesus who sent his disciples to the nations promised to stay with them to the very end — and he is with you too.

topics.title: Contentment
topics.summary: Contentment is learned, not stumbled into. Paul had known plenty and known lack, and in every state he discovered the secret of a satisfied heart. Godliness paired with contentment is true wealth — we came into this world with empty hands, and we'll leave it the same way. Better a little with reverence for God than a fortune wrapped in trouble. He has promised never to leave you nor forsake you; with the Lord as your shepherd, nothing you truly need will be missing.

topics.title: Integrity & Honesty
topics.summary: Integrity is who you are when nobody is checking. Whoever walks uprightly walks securely, but crooked paths always come to light. God takes honesty personally — lying lips are detestable to him, while those who deal truthfully are his delight. Scripture even ties honesty to intimacy: the one who dwells near to God is the one who speaks truth from the heart. So aim to be honest, not only before the Lord but in the eyes of everyone around you. Let integrity be your guide.

topics.title: Courage & Boldness
topics.summary: Courage in Scripture is never self-confidence — it's God-confidence. Joshua was told to be strong and courageous for one reason: the Lord his God would go with him wherever he went. That footing hasn't moved. God hasn't handed us a spirit of fear; he's given power, love, and a sound mind instead. With the Lord as your light and your salvation, who is left to be afraid of? Stand tall. The righteous are as bold as lions.

topics.title: Perseverance
topics.summary: Keeping on when you're tired is where faith gets proven. Scripture pictures the believer's life as a race, one to be run with patience while every weight gets laid aside. Don't grow weary in doing good — the harvest arrives in its proper season if you refuse to quit. Trials work patience in you, patience builds character, and character gives birth to hope. So stand firm, unmoved, always giving yourself to the Lord's work. None of that labor is ever wasted.

topics.title: Envy & Jealousy
topics.summary: Envy eats away at a person from the inside — Scripture calls it rottenness in the bones, while a sound and settled heart gives life. Where jealousy takes root, strife and confusion follow close behind, and often times it starts with a simple glance at what someone else has. Don't fret when the wicked seem to prosper; they fade quickly, like grass in the heat. Ask God for a content heart, one that celebrates others instead of comparing with them.

topics.title: Greed & Covetousness
topics.summary: Your life is not measured by what you own. Jesus warned us to be on guard against covetousness, because the craving for more is a trap — those who chase riches drown themselves in hurtful desires, and whoever loves silver will never have enough of it. God commanded us not to covet for a reason: the heart can only bow to one master. Choose Him over money, and watch contentment do what abundance never could.

topics.title: Idolatry
topics.summary: An idol is anything we place before God — and it doesn't have to be carved from wood or stone. Scripture names even covetousness as idolatry, because whatever owns our desire owns our worship. God's first command is that He alone holds that place. The instruction isn't to manage our idols but to flee them; those who cling to empty things walk away from the mercy that was theirs. Keep yourself for Him alone.

topics.title: Anxiety & Worry
topics.summary: Worry borrows trouble from a tomorrow God is already holding. Jesus points us to the birds — fed daily without storing up a thing — to remind us how carefully our Father watches over His own. Scripture's remedy for anxiety is prayer with thanksgiving, laying every request before God and letting His peace stand guard over your heart and mind. When your thoughts multiply within you, His comfort can still delight your soul. Cast the whole weight on Him. He cares for you.

topics.title: Grief & Loss
topics.summary: God does not stand far off from the grieving. He draws near to the brokenhearted, binding up wounds no one else can see, and He calls those who mourn blessed — because comfort is promised to them. One day He will wipe every tear away, and death and sorrow will be no more. Until then, take heart: our merciful Father comforts us in every trouble so that we, in turn, can comfort someone else walking through theirs.

topics.title: Loneliness
topics.summary: Loneliness is a valley many of us walk through, but you never walk it alone. The Lord goes ahead of you, and He has promised never to fail you or leave you behind. David cried out from his desolation and found mercy; even in the darkest stretch he could say God was with him. And God loves to place the lonely in a family. Jesus' parting promise still stands — He is with you, all the days, to the very end.

topics.title: Persecution
topics.summary: The world's hatred should not catch a believer off guard — Jesus said it hated Him first. Everyone who sets out to live a godly life in Christ will meet opposition somewhere. Don't think it strange when the fiery trial comes. Scripture calls the persecuted blessed and hands them a kingdom, and no distress, danger, or sword can pry you away from Christ's love — in Him we are more than conquerors. Rejoice, for you share in His sufferings now and will share in His glory when it is revealed.

topics.title: Parenting & Children
topics.summary: Children are a gift entrusted to us by the Lord — a heritage, not a burden. Parenting is discipleship at its closest range: teaching God's words diligently at home and along the road, in the sitting down and rising up of everyday life. Start a child on the right path early, and it will stay with him when he's old. Discipline with love, never provoking to anger, but raising them in the instruction of the Lord. Faithful correction today becomes delight and rest tomorrow.

topics.title: Friendship
topics.summary: God designed us to walk through life together. Two fare better than one alone — when one falls, the other is there to lift him up. A true friend loves in every season, sharpening you the way iron sharpens a blade, and to have that kind of friend you must first be one. Above them all stands Jesus, the friend who stays closer than any brother, who showed the greatest love there is by giving His life for those He calls His friends.

topics.title: Generosity
topics.summary: Giving is sowing. Whoever scatters generously will gather a generous harvest, and whoever refreshes others finds himself refreshed. God isn't after reluctant gifts squeezed out of obligation — He loves the giver whose heart is glad in it. When you show kindness to the poor, Scripture says you are lending to the Lord Himself, and He is never in anyone's debt. Jesus taught that the greater blessing belongs to the one giving, not the one receiving. Give freely, and watch how He measures it back.

topics.title: Work & Diligence
topics.summary: Whatever work God has put in your hands, do it with all your heart — you're serving Christ, not merely a boss. Scripture sends the sluggard to study the ant, who needs no overseer to gather her food in its season. Honest labor carries profit where idle talk leads to lack. Diligence has a way of opening doors... the skilled and faithful worker ends up standing before kings. Work wholeheartedly now, in this life, knowing the Lord Himself holds the reward.

topics.title: Serving Others
topics.summary: Jesus, the King of all, knelt down and washed feet — then said He was giving us an example to follow. He didn't come to be waited on; He came to serve, giving His life to ransom many. Our liberty in Christ isn't for indulging ourselves. It's for loving one another through humble service, counting others above ourselves and looking out for their interests too. Whatever you do for the least among us, you have done for Him.

topics.title: Spiritual Gifts
topics.summary: Every believer has received something from the Spirit — the gifts differ, but the Giver is the same. Some teach, some serve, some lead; all of it flows from the one God who works through His people to build up Christ's body. Your gift wasn't handed to you for your own sake. You're a steward of God's varied grace, called to use it in ministering to one another. Discover what He has placed in you, and put it to work for His church.

topics.title: Leadership
topics.summary: In God's kingdom, leadership is turned upside down: whoever wants to be great must become a servant, just as Jesus did. Those who shepherd others are to do it willingly — not for gain, not by lording over anyone, but by living as examples the flock can follow. Scripture looks for leaders who fear God, love truth, and refuse dishonest gain, and it reminds us there is safety in many counselors. When the righteous lead, the people around them flourish.

topics.title: The Cross & Resurrection
topics.summary: The cross and the empty tomb are the center of everything. Christ took the wounds our sins deserved, carried them all the way to the tree, and was laid in a grave that could not hold him. On the third day he rose, just as he promised. And because he lives, we don't stay in the grave of our old ways either — we're raised up with him to walk out a life made completely new. By his wounds, you are healed.

topics.title: Fruit of the Spirit
topics.summary: What grows out of a life is the truest evidence of what's rooted in it. When the Spirit is at work in us, he produces love, joy, peace, patience, and self-control — fruit no law can stand against and no flesh can manufacture. A good tree simply cannot help bearing good fruit. So abide close to Christ and let your life bear fruit in every good thing you do; that's how the Father is glorified, and how the world knows whose disciple you are.

topics.title: Creation
topics.summary: Everything that exists began with God. The skies above you are preaching a sermon every single day, declaring the glory of the one who spoke them into place. All things — seen and unseen — were made by him and made for him, so plainly that no one is left with an excuse. And yet the God who ordained the moon and stars is mindful of you. Look up sometime, and let creation remind you how great he is and how deeply he cares for someone as small as us.

topics.title: God's Faithfulness
topics.summary: His compassions never run dry. Every morning you wake to mercies that weren't there yesterday — fresh, new, and enough for the day ahead. This is the faithful God who keeps his covenant for a thousand generations, the one who called you into fellowship with his Son. Even when our faith wavers, he stays faithful, because he cannot be untrue to himself. His faithfulness reaches past the clouds. Build your life on that.

topics.title: Heaven & Eternal Life
topics.summary: This world is not the end of your story. Jesus has gone ahead to prepare a place, and he promised to come back and bring us to where he is. There, God himself will wipe every tear away — no more death, no more sorrow, no more pain, because the former things will have passed. Our earthly tent may wear out, but a house built by God waits for us, eternal and incorruptible. Whoever believes in the Son will not perish. Hold onto that living hope.

topics.title: The Tongue & Our Words
topics.summary: Your words carry weight — the tongue holds power over both death and life, and we will eat the fruit of whichever we choose to speak. Scripture calls us to be quick to listen and slow to speak, letting nothing leave our lips that doesn't build someone up or minister grace to the one hearing it. A gentle answer can disarm anger before it ever ignites. Make the psalmist's prayer your own: Lord, set a guard over my mouth and keep watch at my lips.

topics.title: Knowing God's Will
topics.summary: God is not hiding his will from you. He promises to instruct, to teach, to guide with his eye upon you — and when you lack wisdom, he gives it generously to everyone who simply asks, without scolding you for asking. Renewing your mind is where discernment begins; a transformed heart learns to recognize what is good and pleasing to him. Plan your way, but hold it loosely. The Lord is the one directing your steps.

topics.title: God's Promises
topics.summary: Not one good word God has spoken has ever fallen to the ground — Israel watched every single promise come to pass, and the same God is keeping his word to you. He is not like us; he cannot lie. What he has said, he will do. Every promise finds its yes and amen in Christ, and through these great, precious promises we're actually made partakers of his own divine nature. Hold fast without wavering, for the one who promised is faithful.

topics.title: Surrender
topics.summary: Surrender is not losing — it's the doorway to really living. Jesus himself prayed it in the garden: not my will, Father, but yours. He calls us to deny ourselves, carry our cross day by day, and follow wherever he leads, offering our whole selves as a living sacrifice. When we're crucified with Christ, someone better lives in our place — Christ himself, living his life through us. Trust him with everything in your heart, lean not on what you understand, and he will direct your path.

topics.title: Waiting on God
topics.summary: Waiting is not wasted when it's spent on the Lord. The season may feel silent, but strength is being renewed in you — the kind that rises up on eagles' wings, that runs and doesn't grow weary. What God has shown you has an appointed time; though it lingers, it is surely coming... So hope in his word. Take courage, and let him strengthen your heart. He is good to every soul who seeks him and quietly waits for his salvation.

topics.title: Walking with God
topics.summary: Enoch walked with God so closely that one day he simply wasn't here anymore — God took him. That's the picture: a daily, humble companionship. The Lord has shown us what he requires — to do justly, love mercy, and walk humbly beside him. Walking in the Spirit keeps us from chasing what the flesh craves, and walking in the light brings us into true fellowship, cleansed by Jesus' own blood. The same way you received Christ, keep walking in him.

topics.title: The Fear of the LORD
topics.summary: To fear the Lord is not to shrink back from him — it's to stand in awe of who he is. Scripture calls this reverence the very starting point of wisdom, a wellspring of life that pulls us back from death's snares. And here is the beautiful part: God shares his secret counsel with those who hold him in awe, showing them his covenant. When everything is said and done, this is the whole of our duty — revere God and hold fast to what he commands.

topics.title: Delighting in God
topics.summary: God isn't merely to be obeyed — he is to be enjoyed. The psalmist calls him my exceeding joy and testifies that in his presence is joy in its fullness, with pleasures that never run out. Delight yourself in the Lord, and watch him reshape and then grant the desires of your heart. Let his word become the thing you meditate on day and night, and he will carry you up to the high places. Joy is part of your inheritance in him.

topics.title: Knowing God
topics.summary: Jesus defined eternal life not as a place but as a person — knowing the one true God and the Son he sent. Paul counted everything else as loss next to the surpassing worth of knowing Christ, and the Lord himself says the only thing worth boasting in is understanding and knowing him. So press on to know him. He meets the one who pursues him as surely as morning comes, refreshing as rain on dry ground. Ask God for a spirit of wisdom and of revelation — he loves to be known.

topics.title: Hearing God's Voice
topics.summary: God still speaks, and his sheep learn the sound of his voice. Often times it comes like a word behind you, pointing out the way when you're deciding whether to turn right or left. Other times it's a knock at the door, waiting for you to open and share the table with him. Answer the way young Samuel did: speak, Lord — your servant is listening. He speaks peace to his people; just don't turn back to folly once you've heard him.

topics.title: First Love
topics.summary: It's possible to serve God faithfully and still drift from loving Him. The Lord remembers the devotion of our early days, and He calls the wandering heart to remember, repent, and return to those first works of love. Sit with the question Jesus pressed on Peter — does your love for Him come before everything else? Nothing this life offers compares to His lovingkindness.

topics.title: Hunger for God
topics.summary: A soul that pants for God like a deer for water streams will not go away empty. Jesus promised that those who hunger and thirst for righteousness shall be filled — and He Himself is the bread that satisfies. Seek Him early. Seek Him in the dry and weary seasons. He fills the hungry heart with goodness, and no appetite He awakens will He leave unmet.

topics.title: Fellowship with God
topics.summary: God has never wanted religion at a distance — He wants communion. Jesus pictures Himself knocking, waiting for anyone who will open the door so He can come in and share a meal. To the one who loves Him and keeps His word, the Father and the Son come and make their home. Grace, love, and the fellowship of the Spirit: this is the life you were invited into.

topics.title: Consecration
topics.summary: Holiness is preparation. When we purge ourselves of what defiles, we become vessels of honor, sanctified and ready for whatever good work the Master has planned. Present your whole body and life to God as a living offering, and refuse to be pressed into this world's mold. Sanctify yourself today — often times it's on the other side of consecration that the Lord does wonders among His people.

topics.title: Following Jesus
topics.summary: Discipleship means walking where Christ walks, whatever it costs. Though we live under the covenant of God's grace and mercy, it is very important that Christians follow Christ– else all the .

topics.title: Friendship with God
topics.summary: Abraham trusted God and was counted righteous — and he came to be known as God's friend. Moses knew the same nearness, speaking with the Lord the way a man speaks with a trusted companion. In Christ, that door swings open for us: Jesus calls His followers friends, not servants, entrusting them with His Father's heart. He is the friend who stays closer than any brother, and He is worth knowing deeply.

topics.title: God's Love for Us
topics.summary: Love didn't start with us. God moved first — sending His only Son so that through Him we might truly live, dying for us while we were still in our sin. His love is everlasting; with lovingkindness He drew you long before you sought Him. And nothing — not death, not life, not things present or things to come — can pry you out of it. He is mighty in your midst, rejoicing over you with singing.

topics.title: Loving God
topics.summary: The first and greatest commandment is not a suggestion: love the Lord your God with everything in you — heart, soul, mind, and strength. This love shows itself in more than feeling. Jesus tied it to obedience: if we love Him, we keep His word. His commandments are no heavy load; they are the glad response of a heart that has made the Lord its strength.

topics.title: Intimacy with God
topics.summary: Seek my face, God says — and the heart that knows Him answers, Your face I will seek. Come near to Him, and He comes near to you; His invitation carries a call to cleansed hands and an undivided heart. Like Moses at the tent, speaking with the Lord as with a friend, we're offered real closeness, not ritual. Abide in Him the way a branch stays joined to the vine, for that is where life flows.

topics.title: Meditation on the Word
topics.summary: Reading the Word and letting it take root are two different things. The one who ponders Scripture day and night grows like a tree set beside streams of water — fruitful in season, with leaves that never wither. Keep His law on your lips and in your thoughts, and your way becomes prosperous in God's timing. May every word of your mouth and every quiet thought be acceptable in His sight; that is where love for His law is formed.

topics.title: Rest in God
topics.summary: Weariness was never meant to be your identity. Jesus calls everyone who labors under heavy burdens to come to Him and find rest for the soul — a rest that means ceasing from your own striving, just as God rested from His works. His presence goes with you. So return to your rest, O soul; the Lord has dealt kindly and generously with you, and He will carry what you cannot.

topics.title: Stillness Before God
topics.summary: Stillness is an act of trust. To be quiet before God is to confess that He is God and we are not — that the battle is His to fight while we hold our peace. Wait on Him alone, and let your expectation come from Him. It is good to hope and wait quietly for His salvation; and in that quiet, He is in your midst, rejoicing over you.

topics.title: Thirst for the Living God
topics.summary: Every soul was made to thirst, and only one fountain runs deep enough. As the deer pants for the stream, the psalmist thirsted after the living God — and Jesus answers that ache with living water, a well inside you springing up into life that never ends. You don't need money to drink. You don't need to earn a place at the waters. The Spirit still says come; whoever is thirsty is welcome, and the drink is free.

topics.title: Union with Christ
topics.summary: The gospel offers more than pardon — it makes you one with Christ Himself. Your old self was crucified with Him; the life you live now is His life in you, and your true life is hidden with Him in God. Joined to the Lord, we become one spirit with Him. So stay in the vine. Cut off from Him we can do nothing, but rooted in Him, the fruit keeps coming.

topics.title: A Living Sacrifice
topics.summary: What can you offer the God who gave you everything? Yourself. By His mercies we're urged to place our whole bodies on the altar as a living offering — not one moment of worship, but a lifetime of it. Christ died so that the living would stop living for themselves. Magnify Him in your body, whether in living or in dying. Bring Him praise as a continual sacrifice, do good, share freely — offerings like these truly please Him.

topics.title: The Secret Place
topics.summary: No storm can reach the one hidden in God. Whoever dwells in His secret place rests beneath the Almighty's shadow, sheltered from prideful men and striving tongues, set high on a rock when trouble rises. So shut the door and pray to your Father in secret — He sees, and He rewards openly. Make Him your refuge and hiding place, and songs of deliverance will rise around you.

topics.title: Drawing Near
topics.summary: God does not hide from those who seek Him. When we move toward Him, He moves toward us — that is His promise. Christ's blood has closed the distance, so hearts once far away can now come with clean hands and full confidence, finding mercy and grace right when they're needed most. Drawing near isn't a ritual; it is the good place your soul was made to live.

topics.title: Humility Before God
topics.summary: The God who inhabits eternity chooses to dwell with the lowly. Pride pushes His grace away, but a humble, broken heart He will never turn from. When you bow low before Him — doing justice, loving mercy, walking humbly — He is the one who does the lifting. You don't have to raise yourself up. Lower yourself in His sight and let Him revive you.

topics.title: Reverence & Awe
topics.summary: Familiarity should never erase the fear of the Lord. He is holy — a consuming fire — and the whole earth is called to stand silent before Him in awe. Scripture teaches us to guard our steps in His house, to be quick to listen and slow to speak, and to worship with reverence rather than rushing in with careless words. Awe is not distance from God; it's the right posture for coming close.

topics.title: Belonging to God
topics.summary: You do not belong to yourself — you were bought at a cost, redeemed and called by name. God made you, He keeps you as a shepherd keeps his sheep, and whether in life or in death you remain His. That's not a loss of freedom; it's the safest place a soul can be. So glorify Him with your body and your spirit, living as one who has been carried from darkness into His light.

topics.title: Chosen by God
topics.summary: Before the world was ever formed, God set His love on you. You didn't find your way to Christ on your own — He chose you first, and He chose you for a purpose: to be holy, to bear fruit that lasts, and to declare His praises as one of His own treasured people. Let that settle any question of your worth. Being chosen isn't something you earned; it's something you carry.

topics.title: Adoption as God's Children
topics.summary: Consider what kind of love this is — the God of heaven has made you His child. Through His Son, He redeemed those under the law so that we could be brought into the family, not as servants afraid of the master, but as sons and daughters who cry out, 'Abba, Father.' His Spirit within confirms it to your spirit. You were adopted on purpose, and it pleased Him to do it.

topics.title: Heirs with Christ
topics.summary: If you are God's child, then you are also His heir — a joint-heir with Christ himself. There is an inheritance waiting for you that cannot rot, fade, or be taken, kept alive because Jesus rose from the grave. Yes, sharing in his glory often times means sharing in his sufferings first. But hold on to that living hope: what has been promised to you was secured by grace, not by your performance.

topics.title: Sealed by the Spirit
topics.summary: When you believed the gospel, God marked you as His own. The Holy Spirit living in you is His seal — a down payment guaranteeing the inheritance still to come. The foundation stands firm: the Lord knows exactly who belongs to Him. So live like someone who's been claimed. Don't grieve the Spirit who sealed you; walk away from sin and toward the redemption day he's keeping you for.

topics.title: Pleasing God
topics.summary: Pleasing God begins with believing Him. Without faith, no amount of effort can satisfy Him — He rewards the ones who seek Him in earnest, not the ones who merely perform. From that faith flows a life that delights Him: a walk that honors the Lord, fruit in every season, a heart still growing to know Him more. Make it your quiet ambition that your words and even your inner thoughts would be acceptable to Him.

topics.title: Walking in the Light
topics.summary: God is light; darkness has no place in Him. To follow Jesus is to leave the shadows behind — he promised that those who walk with him will not stumble in the dark but will carry his light within them. You were darkness once; now you belong to the light. So live openly before Him. Fellowship with God cannot share a room with hidden sin, and His face shines on the path of those who keep step with Him.

topics.title: Wholehearted Devotion
topics.summary: God isn't looking for half of you. His eyes search the whole earth for hearts fully His, so He can show Himself strong on their behalf. A divided heart will always wander, which is why the psalmist prayed for a united one — a single, undistracted love. Seek Him with everything: heart, soul, and mind. His promise stands that when you search for Him with all that's in you, you will find Him.

topics.title: Longing for God's House
topics.summary: The psalmist ached for one thing above everything else — to be where God is. A single day in His presence outweighed a thousand spent anywhere else; he would rather stand at God's doorway than settle down comfortably among the wicked. Does gathering with God's people stir that kind of gladness in you? Ask Him to give you that holy homesickness, the soul-deep longing to behold His beauty and dwell close to Him all your days.

topics.title: Early Seeking
topics.summary: There's something sacred about giving God the first of your day. David directed his prayer heavenward at daybreak. Jesus himself rose long before sunrise to find a quiet place to pray. When we seek the Lord early — before the noise, before the demands — He promises we will find Him, and He wakens our ear morning by morning to hear from Him. Let your soul thirst for Him like dry ground thirsts for water, and bring Him that thirst first.

topics.title: Steadfastness
topics.summary: A fixed heart is an anchored life. When your mind stays settled on the Lord, He keeps you in a peace the news of the day cannot shake — bad tidings lose their power over a heart that trusts Him. So stand firm. Be immovable. Keep abounding in His work, because nothing done for the Lord is ever wasted. And hold your first confidence all the way to the end; that endurance is the mark of those who share in Christ.

topics.title: Clinging to God
topics.summary: Some seasons call for more than casual faith — they call for holding on. Jacob wrestled through the night and refused to release his grip until the blessing came. That's the picture: a soul that follows hard after God while His right hand does the upholding. Cleave to the Lord. Serve Him, obey His voice, and don't loosen your hold when the night feels long. He is holding you far more tightly than you're holding Him.

topics.title: Returning to God
topics.summary: No matter how far you've wandered, the way back is still open. God's plea through the prophets is simple: draw near again, and He will draw near to you. He isn't after torn garments or outward show — He wants the heart, rent and turned toward Him. Like the prodigal, we only have to arise and head home, and we'll find a Father already moving toward us with mercy. Forsake the old way; He pardons abundantly.

topics.title: Renewal of the Mind
topics.summary: Transformation begins in the mind. The world presses us into its mold, but God renews us from the inside out as we fix our thoughts on what is true, pure, and lovely. Every imagination that sets itself against His knowledge can be taken captive and brought under Christ. Guard what you dwell on — where the mind goes, the life follows.

topics.title: God Our Portion
topics.summary: When everything else runs out, God remains. The psalmists learned to call Him their portion — even when flesh and heart give way, He is the strength and inheritance of the soul. Aaron received no land of his own; God was his share. Let that settle in you today. If you have Him, your lot has fallen in a pleasant place, and hope is never far away.

topics.title: The Deity of the Holy Spirit
topics.summary: The Holy Spirit is not a force or a feeling — He is God. When Ananias lied to the Spirit, Peter said he had lied to God Himself. The Spirit searches the deep counsels of God, speaks, calls servants to their work, and can be grieved, because He is a divine Person, not an influence. And wherever He is present, liberty follows. Honor Him as you honor the Father and the Son.

topics.title: The Comforter
topics.summary: Jesus said it was actually better for us that He go away, because the Comforter would come — and stay. The Spirit of truth abides with the believer forever, teaching us, reminding us of everything Jesus said, and always pointing back to Him. The early church walked in that comfort and grew. You were never meant to walk this road alone; the Helper lives within you.

topics.title: Walking in the Spirit
topics.summary: The Christian life isn't powered by willpower — it's led. God promised through Ezekiel to put His own Spirit within His people, moving them to follow His ways from the heart. When we keep in step with Him, the pull of the flesh loses its grip, and no condemnation hangs over us. Those who are led by God's Spirit are His sons and daughters. Follow His lead today.

topics.title: The Spirit's Power
topics.summary: God's work has never depended on human muscle. Not by might, not by strength, but by His Spirit — that's how His purposes move forward. Jesus told His disciples to wait until power came down from heaven before going out as witnesses, and that same Spirit still strengthens the inner man today. Whatever He's called you to, don't attempt it in your own energy. Ask to be filled.

topics.title: Grieving the Spirit
topics.summary: The Spirit of God can be grieved — let that sober us. Bitterness, wrath, harsh words, a stubborn and resistant heart: often times it's these everyday things that vex the very One who sealed us for redemption. Israel learned it the hard way. Don't quench His fire or resist His voice. Like David, pray that God would keep His presence near, and deal quickly with whatever grieves Him.

topics.title: The New Birth
topics.summary: Nicodemus came with questions, and Jesus gave him the answer beneath them all: you must be born again. Religion can polish the outside, but only the Spirit can birth new life within — a heart of flesh where the heart of stone used to be. In Christ, the old has passed and everything is made new, planted by a seed that can never perish: the living word of God. Have you been born from above?

topics.title: Justification by Faith
topics.summary: Peace with God is not earned — it's received. Scripture is emphatic that no amount of law-keeping can justify us; we're declared righteous freely, by grace, through trusting in Christ. To the one who stops working to prove himself and simply believes, faith is counted as righteousness. Rest here. Your standing before God depends on His finished work, not your unfinished one.

topics.title: Sanctification
topics.summary: Sanctification is God's stated will for your life — being set apart, made holy in body, soul, and spirit. It happens slowly and surely: as we behold the Lord's glory in His word of truth, the Spirit changes us into His image, one degree of glory at a time. And here's the comfort: the same offering that saved you has already secured your completion. He who began the work will finish it.

topics.title: Redemption
topics.summary: You were bought at a price no silver or gold could match — the blood of Christ Himself, a lamb spotless and pure. He took the curse that belonged to us so we could be freed from every iniquity, delivered out of darkness, and brought into His dear Son's kingdom. Redemption isn't only a rescue; it's a claim. You belong now to the One who purchased you — set apart, and zealous for good works.

topics.title: Reconciliation
topics.summary: We were not neutral toward God — we were enemies, alienated in our minds by wicked works. Yet while the hostility was still ours, God moved toward us, reconciling us to Himself through His Son's death and refusing to count our trespasses against us. The cross slew the enmity. Now we stand at peace with Him, presented blameless in His sight, and entrusted to carry that same message of peace to others.

topics.title: Atonement
topics.summary: Long before the cross, God taught His people that sin costs life — blood given on the altar to cover the soul, for without it there is no remission. Every sacrifice pointed forward to Christ, who appeared once, in these last days, to deal with sin fully by giving Himself. He is the satisfying sacrifice, and not for our sins alone but for the whole world. The debt is paid. Draw near.

topics.title: The Lamb of God
topics.summary: John saw Jesus approaching and announced Him as God's own Lamb — the one come to carry the world's sin away. Isaiah foresaw Him too: oppressed and afflicted, yet silent, led to slaughter like a spotless lamb. This was no accident of history; He was slain in God's plan from before the world's foundation. And heaven now sings what earth once despised — the slain Lamb is worthy of power, riches, wisdom, and honor. Behold Him, and worship.

topics.title: The Good Shepherd
topics.summary: Jesus doesn't lead his flock from a distance. He knows each of his sheep, and they recognize his voice when he calls. He laid down his own life so that not one of them would perish, and no one can pry them from his grasp. If you've wandered, take heart. The Shepherd of your soul is still calling you back. Follow close to him, and you will lack nothing.

topics.title: The Bread of Life
topics.summary: Everything this world feeds us leaves us hungry again. Jesus offers something different– himself, the living bread sent down from heaven to give life to the world. Just as God humbled Israel with manna to teach them dependence, he reminds us that we don't survive on bread alone, but on every word he speaks. Come to Christ and your soul will not go hungry. Believe on him, and the deepest thirst you carry will finally be satisfied.

topics.title: The Light of the World
topics.summary: Darkness cannot overcome him. Isaiah saw it coming centuries beforehand. A great light would dawn on people sitting in death's shadow, and in Jesus that light has come. It still shines on every heart that turns to him. You don't have to stumble through life blind. Follow him, and darkness loses its claim on you; his light becomes the light you live by.

topics.title: The True Vine
topics.summary: A branch cut off from the vine withers; it simply cannot produce anything on its own. Neither can we. Jesus calls us to remain in him the way a branch stays joined to the vine, letting his life flow into ours until fruit appears: love, joy, peace, patience, gentleness, and all the rest. The Father is glorified when our lives grow heavy with that harvest. So stay connected. Fruit was never meant to come from your own straining, but from his life moving through you.

topics.title: The Way, the Truth, and the Life
topics.summary: There is no back-up plan for salvation. Jesus is the only way to the Father, the only name given under heaven by which anyone can be saved. Through his own flesh, torn like the veil, he opened a living way into God's presence. Whoever has the Son has life. It really is that simple, and that serious. Stop searching for another door. There isn't one, and thankfully, this one is enough.

topics.title: Christ Our Mediator
topics.summary: Between a holy God and fallen humanity stands one mediator: Jesus Christ, himself a man. His death purchased redemption under a new covenant, and his work didn't end at the cross. He lives even now at the Father's right hand, praying on our behalf. When you sin, you have an advocate. When accusation comes, he answers it. He is able to save completely everyone who comes to God through him, because his intercession for you never stops.

topics.title: Christ Our High Priest
topics.summary: Our high priest is not cold toward our weakness. Jesus was made like his brethren in every way and tempted in all points as we are, so that he could be merciful and faithful in reconciling us to God. He learned obedience through suffering, and now– holy, undefiled, exalted above the heavens– he is seated beside the throne of Majesty on our behalf. So hold fast to your confession. The one representing you before God knows exactly what your struggle feels like.

topics.title: The Incarnation
topics.summary: At just the right moment in history, God sent his Son. The eternal Word took on flesh and made his home among us– Emmanuel, God with us. Though he was equal with God, he emptied himself, taking a servant's form and entering our likeness as a baby born under the law. This is the good news the angel announced: a Savior had come, not to observe our condition from a distance but to step into it. Grace and truth now have a face.

topics.title: The Ascension
topics.summary: The story didn't end at the empty tomb. After purging our sins, Jesus was taken up before his disciples' eyes and seated at God's right hand, far above every ruler, power, and name that can be named. His ascension is not his absence. Exalted and reigning, he now fills all things, and the same Jesus who rose through the clouds is the one who will return. Until then he governs from the throne, and nothing sits higher than him.

topics.title: The Names of Jesus
topics.summary: Every name Scripture gives him reveals another facet of who he is. Wonderful. Counsellor. Prince of Peace. King over all kings and Lord over all lords. The name Jesus itself carries his mission, for he came to save his own from sin's grip, and God has exalted that name higher than any other. One day every knee will bend at the sound of it. No other name under heaven can save; learn to treasure his.

topics.title: Jesus Our Example
topics.summary: Christ didn't only die for us– he showed us how to live. He suffered without retaliation, served without demanding recognition, and knelt to wash the feet of men who would soon abandon him. If we claim to abide in him, our walk ought to look like his. Fix your eyes on Jesus, who endured the cross for the joy ahead of him, and let his mind become the pattern for yours. Then follow, step by step, in his footprints.

topics.title: The Compassion of Jesus
topics.summary: Often times we imagine God as distant from human pain, but the Gospels show us otherwise. When Jesus saw the crowds wandering like sheep with no one to lead them, his heart was moved. He touched the leper no one else would touch. He stopped for a grieving widow and told her not to weep. That compassion has not cooled. Our high priest still feels the weight of our weaknesses, so bring him yours. He is not indifferent to what you're carrying.

topics.title: The Miracles of Jesus
topics.summary: The miracles were never just displays of power. Blind eyes opened, lepers were made clean, and Lazarus walked out of his own tomb; each work bore witness that the Father truly sent him. God confirmed Jesus publicly through wonders and signs, and John tells us plainly why these accounts were written down: so that we might believe he is the Christ, and believing, find life in his name. The miracles still preach. Let them lead you to the one who performed them.

topics.title: The Teachings of Jesus
topics.summary: Even the officers sent to arrest him returned empty-handed, admitting no one had ever spoken the way he did. Jesus taught with an authority the scribes couldn't imitate, and the crowds were astonished at it. His words are more than good teaching. They carry spirit and life within them. But hearing isn't enough. The one who hears his sayings and does them is like a wise builder setting his house on rock. When the storms beat against it, it stands. Build your life on what he said.

topics.title: The Second Coming
topics.summary: The angels said it plainly: the same Jesus who rose into heaven will return just as he left. He has gone ahead to make a place ready for his own, and he is coming back to receive us to himself. One day the shout will sound, those who died in Christ will rise, and we will be gathered to him forever. This is our blessed hope– not a vague wish, but a promise from the one who says he comes quickly, bringing his reward with him. Live ready. Live looking up.

topics.title: The Intercession of Christ
topics.summary: Jesus is praying for you right now. He lives forever at the Father's right hand, pleading on behalf of everyone who comes to God through him. When Satan asked to sift Peter, Christ had already prayed that his faith would hold — and often times that is exactly what he is doing for you in your weakest hour. Even when you stumble, you have an Advocate, the Righteous One himself. The same Jesus who died for you now speaks for you.

topics.title: Christ in You
topics.summary: The great mystery of the gospel is not merely that we go to be with God, but that Christ himself comes to live in us. His life becomes ours — the old self crucified, and a new life lived by faith in the Son who loved us and gave everything. Let him dwell deeply in your heart, rooted in love, and examine yourself honestly to see that this hope of glory is truly at work in you.

topics.title: The Blood of the Covenant
topics.summary: Every covenant God makes, he seals — and the new covenant is sealed in the blood of Jesus, poured out so that sin could be fully forgiven. That blood does more than pardon; it purges the conscience of dead works and frees us to serve a living God. Each time we take the cup in remembrance, we recall that the same God who raised our great Shepherd from the dead is still at work in us, shaping us into people who carry out his will.

topics.title: The Gift of the Spirit
topics.summary: The Holy Spirit is not earned — he is given.
