When his calling was questioned, God settled it Himself — a dead rod budded, blossomed, and bore almonds overnight. From his lips came the blessing still spoken over God's people: the LORD keeping, shining, giving peace. God confirms those He appoints, and He puts words of blessing in the mouths of His servants. Use yours to bless.

topics.title: Miriam
topics.summary: Miriam watched over her baby brother at the river's edge, and years later led Israel's women in songs of victory at the sea. God Himself names her among the leaders He sent before His people. Yet her story carries a warning too — when she spoke against Moses out of jealousy, it cost her dearly. The gifts God gives are for lifting His name and serving His people, never for exalting ourselves. Sing His triumph; leave the pride behind.

topics.title: Joshua
topics.summary: When Moses' time ended, God raised up Joshua and told him again and again to be strong and full of courage — because the LORD Himself would go with him. Walls collapsed at a shout. A river stood still at the priests' feet. And at the end of his days, Joshua laid the choice before the people: decide today whom you will serve. That same choice sits before you. Be courageous, and serve the LORD with your whole house.

topics.title: Caleb
topics.summary: While ten spies saw giants, Caleb saw a God bigger than all of them. He was a man marked by another spirit — one that followed the LORD wholly, without reserve. Forty-five years of wilderness and waiting didn't dim his fire; at eighty-five he was still ready to take the land God had promised him. Wholehearted devotion doesn't expire with age or hardship. Follow God fully, and hold on until He brings you into His promise.

topics.title: Rahab
topics.summary: Rahab's past didn't disqualify her future. A harlot in a doomed city, she heard what God had done and believed He was God of heaven above and earth below — then she acted on it, hiding the spies at great risk. Her faith saved her whole household, and she found a lasting place among God's people. No history is too broken for grace. Believe Him, act on that belief, and watch Him write you into His story.

topics.title: Deborah
topics.summary: In a dark season for Israel, God raised up Deborah — a prophetess who judged the nation from under a palm tree and arose as a mother to her people. When Barak hesitated, she went with him, certain the LORD had already gone out ahead of the army. Her confidence wasn't in herself; it was in the God who goes before. When He calls you forward, rise. The battle belongs to the One already out in front.

topics.title: Gideon
topics.summary: God greeted Gideon as a mighty warrior while he was still hiding from the enemy. He felt like the least of the weakest family, but the LORD's answer settled everything — He had sent him, and He would be with him. Then God shrank his army to three hundred so no one could take the credit. Your weakness isn't the obstacle you think it is. It's often the very place God chooses to display His strength.

topics.title: Samson
topics.summary: Set apart to God from the womb, Samson carried strength no man could match — yet he treated his consecration carelessly, and it cost him his eyes, his freedom, and his calling. Even so, the story doesn't end in the prison house. When he called on the LORD one last time, God answered. Guard what God has set apart in you. And if you've squandered it, know this: He still hears the prayer of a returning heart.

topics.title: Ruth
topics.summary: Ruth chose covenant loyalty when walking away would have been easier. A Moabite widow, she bound herself to Naomi and to Naomi's God, gleaning in another man's field with nothing to her name. God saw. He provided a redeemer in Boaz, and He wove her story straight into the lineage of Jesus. Your faithfulness in obscurity is never wasted — God honors those who cling to Him and to the people He has given them.

topics.title: Naomi
topics.summary: Bitterness ran so deep that Naomi asked to be called by another name. She went out full and came home feeling emptied of everything. Yet God had not abandoned her. Through Ruth's loyalty and a kinsman-redeemer, the Lord restored her life and placed a grandson in her arms. If this season has emptied you, take heart. The God who seems silent is still writing, and He delights to turn mourning into fullness.

topics.title: Boaz
topics.summary: Boaz used his strength and wealth to shelter the vulnerable instead of exploiting them. He noticed a foreign widow gleaning at the edges of his field, protected her, and paid the full price to redeem her — publicly, before witnesses. In him we glimpse Christ, our Kinsman-Redeemer, who bought us for Himself. Whatever influence God has placed in your hands, it was given so someone else could find refuge under it.

topics.title: Hannah
topics.summary: Hannah carried her deepest ache straight to the Lord — weeping, vowing, pouring out her soul in prayer. God remembered her. And when He gave her Samuel, she gave him right back, holding the answer with open hands. Her story teaches us to bring our longing to God rather than nurse it alone, and to worship Him as the giver and not just for the gift. He is faithful to those who wait on Him in prayer.

topics.title: Samuel
topics.summary: From childhood, Samuel learned to answer God's voice with a servant's ear — and he never stopped listening. God stayed near him, and his words carried weight because they were God's words first. He judged Israel, he prophesied, he anointed kings, and he counted it sin to stop praying for the people. A life of quiet, steady obedience leaves a mark no title can. Stay listening. Stay faithful.

topics.title: Saul
topics.summary: Outwardly, Saul had everything — stature, appearance, a kingdom handed to him through God's own anointing. But partial obedience unraveled it all. God delights in a heart that obeys more than in sacrifices offered on our own terms, and Saul's refusal to listen cost him the throne and, in the end, his life. Let his story search you. Giftedness can open doors; only obedience keeps you walking with God through them.

topics.title: David
topics.summary: Overlooked by men and chosen by God — that was David from the start. A shepherd boy anointed while his brothers stood by, he faced a giant with no armor but his God's name. He also fell hard into sin, yet ran back to mercy with a broken and honest heart. That is what made him a man after God's heart: not perfection, but repentance and trust. And through his line came the King whose throne truly stands forever.

topics.title: Jonathan
topics.summary: Few friendships in Scripture run as deep as Jonathan's love for David. His covenant loyalty cost him everything, including his own claim to a throne. He trusted that God is never limited by numbers, and when David was hunted in the wilderness, Jonathan went to him and pointed him back to the strength found in God alone. That is what godly friendship looks like. Be the friend who strengthens another soul in the Lord, even when it costs you.

topics.title: Solomon
topics.summary: Solomon asked God for an understanding heart, and the Lord gave him wisdom beyond any man of his day. He built the temple. He wrote of life's vanity apart from God. Yet in old age his heart drifted after other gods, turned little by little by divided loves. His story is a sober one: the wisest beginning cannot replace a guarded heart. Ask God for wisdom — then keep your heart wholly His to the end.

topics.title: Elijah
topics.summary: Elijah stood alone before kings and called down fire, yet Scripture is careful to tell us he was a man with passions just like ours. His power was not in his personality — it was in earnest prayer to a living God. And when he was worn thin, God met him not in the wind or the fire, but in a quiet whisper. Pray boldly. And when you are spent, listen closely; God often speaks softest when you need Him most.

topics.title: Elisha
topics.summary: When the mantle fell on him, Elisha left his oxen and never looked back. He dared to ask for double the spirit that rested on Elijah, and God answered — oil that would not run out, a leper made clean, a dead boy breathing again. Miracle after miracle flowed through a man who simply left everything to follow. What are you still holding onto? Full surrender is the doorway to seeing God move.

topics.title: Job
topics.summary: Job lost everything in a day and still bowed to worship, blessing the God who gives and takes away. He did not have answers — he had trust, the kind that holds on even when hope seems fatal. Through the ache, he came to know God by sight and not by rumor, and the Lord restored him double when he prayed for his friends. Suffering has an end, and the God on the other side of it is worth knowing.

topics.title: Isaiah
topics.summary: One vision of God enthroned undid Isaiah completely. Seeing the Lord's holiness, he saw his own uncleanness — and once God touched and cleansed his lips, his answer came quickly: send me. From that surrendered life flowed the clearest pictures of Christ in the Old Testament, the suffering servant who carried our griefs, the child born to reign in peace. See Him rightly, and you will go wherever He sends.

topics.title: Jeremiah
topics.summary: Before Jeremiah drew his first breath, God knew him and set him apart. His calling cost him dearly — he wept over his people and was tempted to quit — but the word blazed in his bones like a fire he could not hold in. Even in the ruins of Jerusalem, he found the Lord's mercies arriving fresh with the morning. God's faithfulness meets you in the wreckage too. What He has called you to carry, He will give you grace to keep speaking.

topics.title: Ezekiel
topics.summary: Ezekiel saw the heavens open while sitting among captives — proof that exile cannot cut you off from the presence of God. Appointed a watchman, he spoke hard truth to a rebellious people, and in a valley of scattered bones he watched God's breath do what no human effort could. The Lord still promises what He promised then: a stony heart exchanged for a living one. Nothing is too dead for Him. Speak what He gives you, and trust His Spirit to bring the life.

topics.title: Daniel
topics.summary: Daniel settled his convictions before the pressure ever arrived, choosing purity in a pagan palace. His is a faith that didn't hide — windows open, kneeling in prayer morning, noon, and night even when it could cost him his life. God honored that steadfastness, revealing what no wise man could and shutting the mouths of hungry lions. Decide now, in your heart, whom you will serve. A life anchored like Daniel's shines, and it turns others toward righteousness.

topics.title: Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego
topics.summary: Three men stood while everyone else bowed, trusting that the God they served could deliver them — and resolving that even if He didn't, they still would not bow. When the flames came they were not alone; a fourth man walked with them, and the fire couldn't so much as singe them. You may face a furnace of your own for standing firm. Stand anyway. Christ meets His people in the middle of the fire, and even kings take notice when God delivers His trusting servants.

topics.title: Nehemiah
topics.summary: Before he ever carried a plan to the king, Nehemiah carried his burden to God — weeping, fasting, and praying over a city in ruins. Then, when the moment came, he breathed a quick prayer and spoke up. What followed shows what God can do through willing hearts: hands strengthened for the work, a wall rebuilt in fifty-two days, and enemies forced to admit that God was behind it. Bring your burdens to Him first. He knows how to turn mourning into building.

topics.title: Ezra
topics.summary: There's an order in Ezra's life worth copying: he prepared himself to seek God's word, to live it out, and only then to teach it — and the good hand of God rested on him for it. Rather than lean on a king's soldiers, he fasted and sought the Lord for protection on the journey. When the people gathered to hear the law, it wasn't merely read; it was explained until they understood. Let Scripture shape you first. Then help others grasp the sense of it too.

topics.title: Esther
topics.summary: An orphan raised in exile became a queen positioned to save a nation — and none of it was chance. When the threat came, Esther didn't rush ahead in her own strength; she fasted, called her people to fast with her, and then risked her life to intercede for them. Consider where God has placed you. The position you hold may exist for a moment only you can meet. Walk in it with courage, and watch Him turn sorrow into gladness and mourning into light.

topics.title: Mordecai
topics.summary: Faithfulness rarely needs a spotlight. Mordecai served quietly in a foreign court, refused to bow where worship didn't belong, and spoke hard truth to Esther when silence would have been easier. In due time, the honor Haman craved for himself was draped on Mordecai instead. Live like that — unbending before what is wrong, honest with the people you love, seeking the good of those around you. God sees the quiet ones, and He exalts them in His own timing.

topics.title: Jonah
topics.summary: You cannot outrun the God who made the sea. Jonah tried, and grace pursued him all the way down — yet from the deepest place a man could pray, God still heard his cry. What convicts most is why he ran: Jonah knew the Lord was gracious and didn't want that mercy reaching his enemies. Search your own heart here. Is there anyone you've quietly decided is beyond compassion? Our God is slow to anger, and His mercy runs wider than we would ever draw it.

topics.title: Jonah's Great Fish
topics.summary: The great fish wasn't punishment — it was provision, prepared by God to catch a drowning runaway. Even the depths obey His voice. Jesus pointed to those three days in the deep as a picture of His own death and resurrection, meaning Jonah's rescue was preaching the gospel centuries before the cross. When your soul grows faint, remember the Lord. Salvation belongs to Him alone, and He can raise life up out of any pit.

topics.title: Josiah
topics.summary: Still young, Josiah began seeking the God of David — proof that no heart is too young to turn fully to the Lord. When the neglected law was read aloud to him, he didn't defend himself; he tore his clothes and humbled his heart. That tenderness toward God's word fueled a reformation that swept the idols out of the land, and Scripture says no king before or after turned to God quite like him. Let the word cut you that deeply. A heart soft enough to grieve over sin is one God will use.

topics.title: Hezekiah
topics.summary: When a threatening letter arrived, Hezekiah didn't panic or scheme — he spread it out before the Lord and prayed. That was the pattern of his whole life: he clung to God and refused to let go, and God answered by defeating an army no man could touch and adding years to a life that seemed finished. Whatever letter you're holding today, lay it open before Him. He has heard your prayer. He has seen your tears. He is not done with you yet.

topics.title: Jehoshaphat
topics.summary: Outnumbered and afraid, Jehoshaphat turned his fear into seeking. He gathered the people to fast and admitted openly that he had no strength and no plan — only eyes fixed on God. Then came the remarkable part: singers were sent out ahead of the army, and praise marched first into battle. The fight in front of you may not be yours to win at all. Keep your eyes on Him, worship on the way, and let God be the one who does the fighting.

topics.title: Ruth's Redeemer Line
topics.summary: A Moabite widow gleaning in a Bethlehem field became the great-grandmother of King David — and a name in the very lineage of Christ. On purpose, God wove outsiders like Ruth and Rahab into His plan of redemption. Nothing in your past places you outside His story. The everlasting Ruler promised from little Bethlehem came through unlikely people, and He still delights to graft the overlooked into His family by faith.

topics.title: Melchizedek
topics.summary: Melchizedek steps into Scripture briefly — a king of Salem and priest of God Most High, blessing Abraham with bread and wine — then the record falls silent for centuries. Yet God swore that His Messiah would hold a priesthood of that same unending order. This mysterious king of righteousness and peace points us straight to Jesus, whose priesthood never expires. Take comfort in that. You have an intercessor who will never retire, never fail, and never be replaced.

topics.title: Lot
topics.summary: Choosing by sight cost Lot dearly. He pitched his life toward a city that nearly consumed him, and even as judgment fell he lingered — until God, in mercy, took him by the hand and pulled him out. His wife looked back, and Jesus tells us plainly to remember her. Take stock of what you're choosing on appearances alone, and of what your heart keeps turning back toward. When God delivers you from something, don't camp at its edges.

topics.title: Jacob's Twelve Sons
topics.summary: Twelve brothers from one complicated household — marked by rivalry, jealousy, and real failure — became the tribes that carried Israel's name. Jacob blessed each son individually, each according to what God had for him, and their names echo all the way into Revelation's sealed multitude. That is how our God works. He doesn't wait for a perfect family to build His purposes; He takes flawed people and carries His promise through them, generation after generation.

topics.title: The Virgin Mary
topics.summary: Mary teaches us what surrender looks like. When God's plan interrupted her life, she yielded to His word and answered with worship. She wasn't chosen for her status — God looked upon her lowliness and lifted her up. Like Mary, treasure what the Lord is doing in your life and ponder it quietly in your heart, even the parts you don't yet understand. He honors the humble who simply say yes to Him.

topics.title: Joseph, Husband of Mary
topics.summary: Not one word of Joseph's is recorded in Scripture, yet his obedience speaks volumes. A just man, he chose mercy when he could have chosen shame, and every time God spoke — take Mary home, flee to Egypt — he rose and did it. Some of us are called to serve like Joseph: quietly, faithfully, without applause. God sees that kind of obedience, and He builds His greatest works upon it.

topics.title: John the Baptist
topics.summary: John's whole life pointed away from himself. Sent to prepare hearts through repentance, he was quick to step aside the moment Jesus arrived — content for Christ to grow greater while he grew smaller. Jesus called him the greatest among those born of women, yet John never sought the spotlight. That's the calling for us too. Let your life be a voice that turns people toward the Lamb who carries sin away.

topics.title: Peter
topics.summary: Peter shows us that failure is never the end of the story with Jesus. The same man who boldly confessed Jesus as the Christ denied Him three times and wept over it bitterly. But the Lord sought him out, restored him with patient love, and handed him a flock to feed. That restored man stood up at Pentecost and preached without fear. If you've fallen, take heart — Christ isn't finished with you. Time spent with Him is what makes ordinary, unlearned people bold.

topics.title: Andrew
topics.summary: Andrew's gift was bringing people to Jesus. The first thing he did after finding the Messiah was go get his brother — and that brother was Peter. Later he brought a boy with a small lunch, and Jesus fed a multitude with it. When Greeks wanted to meet the Lord, they came through Andrew too. You don't need a platform to change lives. Simply introduce people to Christ, and watch what He does with whatever you bring Him.

topics.title: James and John
topics.summary: Jesus nicknamed these brothers sons of thunder, and they lived up to it — bold enough to ask for thrones beside Him in glory. But walking with Christ reshaped that fire. James became the first apostle to lay down his life for the faith, and John became known simply as the disciple Jesus loved. Bring your ambition to the Lord. He won't crush it; He'll redirect it toward a cup worth drinking and a love worth everything.

topics.title: Thomas
topics.summary: Thomas gets remembered for his doubt, but look at how Jesus handled it. He didn't shame Thomas — He met him, showed His wounds, and invited him to believe. Thomas answered with one of the greatest confessions in Scripture, calling Jesus his Lord and his God. Honest questions don't disqualify you. Bring them to Christ. And remember His words there: blessed are those who trust Him without ever seeing Him with their eyes.

topics.title: Matthew
topics.summary: Matthew was sitting in a tax booth — a despised man in a despised trade — when Jesus walked by and called him. He rose, left it all behind, and then threw a dinner so his fellow outcasts could meet the Lord too. The religious grumbled, but Jesus made it plain that He came for sinners, not for those who think they're well. Your past doesn't disqualify you from His call. It often times becomes the very table where others meet Him.

topics.title: Philip the Apostle
topics.summary: Philip was found before he found anyone — Jesus sought him out and simply said to follow. His first instinct was to go tell Nathanael, answering skepticism with an invitation to come see for himself. Yet Philip was still learning; years in, he asked Jesus to reveal the Father, not yet grasping that he'd been looking at Him all along. Keep following even while your understanding catches up. And keep inviting others along the way.

topics.title: Nathanael
topics.summary: Nathanael came to Jesus a skeptic, wondering out loud whether anything good could come from Nazareth. Jesus wasn't offended by the question. He revealed that He'd already seen Nathanael beneath the fig tree before Philip ever called him — and being fully known turned the doubter into a worshiper on the spot. God sees you right where you sit, long before you ever seek Him. Come with your questions, and He will show you far greater things than you imagine.

topics.title: Judas Iscariot
topics.summary: Judas walked beside Jesus for years and still sold Him for silver. His story is a sober warning that nearness to Christ is not the same as surrender to Him. Secret sin — for Judas, a love of money fed in the dark — will grow until it betrays with a kiss. And worldly sorrow, unlike true repentance, only led him to despair. Guard your heart while it's still today. Bring what's hidden into the light before it brings you down.

topics.title: Mary Magdalene
topics.summary: Mary Magdalene knew exactly what Jesus had delivered her from — seven devils had once held her — and her gratitude became devotion. She stayed near the cross when others fled, and she was at the tomb weeping before sunrise. So the risen Lord chose her, first of anyone, to see Him alive and carry the news. Those who have been forgiven much love much. Let your deliverance turn into devotion, and He will entrust you with more than you'd dare ask.

topics.title: Mary and Martha
topics.summary: These two sisters loved Jesus in different ways — Martha through busy hands, Mary from a seat at His feet. When Martha's serving turned to worry, Jesus gently told her that only one thing was truly needed, and Mary had chosen it. Yet it was Martha who later confessed Him as the Christ, and Mary who poured out costly ointment in worship. Serve Him, yes... but never let the serving crowd out simply sitting with Him and hearing His word.

topics.title: Lazarus
topics.summary: The story of Lazarus holds two wonders side by side: Jesus wept at His friend's grave, then called the dead man out of it. Our Lord feels sorrow with you even when He already knows how He'll redeem it. He declared that resurrection, and life itself, are found in Him — whoever believes will live even beyond dying. Whatever feels dead in your life, His delay is not His absence. When He speaks, the graveclothes come off.

topics.title: Zacchaeus
topics.summary: Zacchaeus was a wealthy man with an empty, seeking heart — so desperate to see Jesus that he climbed a tree just for a glimpse. Jesus stopped, called him by name, and invited Himself in, while the crowd murmured about the company He kept. One encounter changed everything: half his goods to the poor, fourfold repayment to anyone he'd wronged. Christ came seeking the lost, and when He finds you, generosity and joy follow close behind.

topics.title: Nicodemus
topics.summary: Nicodemus came to Jesus under cover of darkness, a respected teacher carrying honest questions. Jesus met him there with the heart of the gospel– a birth from above, and a Father whose love gave His only Son so that believers would never perish. Watch the journey: from a nighttime conversation, to defending Jesus before the council, to openly honoring Him at the cross. Faith often times starts small and hidden. Bring your questions to Christ; He can grow a secret seed into bold devotion.

topics.title: The Samaritan Woman
topics.summary: At an ordinary well on an ordinary day, Jesus offered a weary woman water that would end her thirst forever. He knew everything she had ever done, and He stayed in the conversation anyway, revealing Himself plainly as the Messiah. She left her jar behind, ran to tell her city, and many believed through her testimony. Jesus knows your whole story too. Let Him satisfy the thirst underneath it all, then go tell somebody what He has done.

topics.title: Stephen
topics.summary: Stephen was chosen to wait on tables, yet he ministered in wonder-working power, filled with faith and with the Spirit. When the stones began to fly, he looked up and saw Jesus standing at the Father's right hand– and with his dying breath he asked God to forgive the very men killing him. That is what a heart saturated with Christ looks like. Fix your gaze on heaven, and grace will pour out of you even in your hardest hour.

topics.title: Philip the Evangelist
topics.summary: Philip started out distributing bread to widows and ended up carrying the gospel wherever the Spirit placed him. He preached Christ to a whole city, then left the crowds to explain the Scriptures to one searching traveler on a desert road. Years later we find him still at it, hosting the saints in his home. Be available like that. God uses the willing– for the multitude and for the one.

topics.title: Barnabas
topics.summary: The apostles renamed Joses the son of encouragement, and he spent the rest of his life living up to it... Barnabas gave his land freely, vouched for Saul when every other believer kept their distance, and urged a young church to cling to the Lord with all their heart. He even fought for Mark's second chance. Who around you needs someone in their corner? Be the one who notices grace at work and says so.

topics.title: Paul the Apostle
topics.summary: On the road to Damascus, a blinding light stopped the church's fiercest persecutor in his tracks, and grace remade him into its boldest missionary. Paul never got over that mercy. He counted himself least among the apostles, yet became a chosen vessel carrying the name of Jesus to nations and kings. If the Lord could turn Saul into Paul, nobody in your life is too far gone. Run your race like he did, and finish still holding the faith.

topics.title: Timothy
topics.summary: Timothy grew up on the Scriptures, taught first at home by a faithful mother and grandmother whose sincere faith took root in him. Paul found in him a rare heart: a young man who genuinely cared for the church while so many were chasing their own interests. Never let anyone dismiss you for your youth or quiet beginnings. Set the example in how you speak, love, believe, and live, and continue in what you have learned.

topics.title: Silas
topics.summary: Beaten, shackled, and dropped into a dark cell for preaching the gospel, Silas answered midnight with a song. His praise rose where complaining would have been understandable, and the prisoners around him heard every note. Worship is a choice you can make in any circumstance. When your midnight comes, sing anyway; you never know who is listening, or what chains God is about to shake loose.

topics.title: Priscilla and Aquila
topics.summary: Priscilla and Aquila show us what a marriage yoked to Christ can do. They worked a trade with their hands, opened their home until a church was meeting inside it, and quietly took a gifted preacher aside to help him understand God's way more completely. They even risked their necks for Paul's sake. Your house, your work, your marriage– every ordinary thing you have can become a place where the gospel grows.

topics.title: Apollos
topics.summary: Eloquent and mighty in his handling of Scripture, Apollos showed his greatness most in his teachability: he let two humble tentmakers pull him aside and fill in what he was missing. Gifting and humility together made him fruitful. But remember what Paul said: one plants, another waters, and it is God who gives the growth. Stay teachable, use your gift fervently, and give Him all the credit.

topics.title: Lydia
topics.summary: By a riverside in Philippi, a dealer in purple cloth listened as Paul spoke, and the Lord opened her heart to receive the gospel. Lydia's response was immediate: she was baptized with her household and insisted the missionaries stay under her roof. Soon her home became the place where the brethren gathered and were comforted. Salvation begins with God opening hearts. Ours is to answer like Lydia did, with open doors and swift obedience.

topics.title: Cornelius
topics.summary: Before Cornelius ever heard the gospel preached, heaven had already taken note of him: his prayers and his generosity rose before God as a memorial. So God sent Peter to his door, and while the word was still being spoken, the Spirit fell on everyone listening. God shows no partiality; in every nation the one who fears Him and does right is received. Keep seeking Him. He sees, and He will meet you with more of Himself.

topics.title: Dorcas (Tabitha)
topics.summary: Dorcas never preached a sermon that we know of– she sewed. When she died, the widows of Joppa stood weeping, holding up garments her hands had stitched for them. Her quiet service mattered so much that God raised her to life again through Peter's prayer, and many in the city believed. Faith that is real gets busy. Let yours show up in meals, mending, and small kindnesses, the kind of love people can hold in their hands.

topics.title: Titus
topics.summary: Titus carried a beautiful reputation: when he showed up, downcast hearts were lifted. Paul called him a true son and a trusted partner, and admitted he had no rest of spirit when Titus was missing. That is why he handed him the hard assignment of setting a struggling church in order. Be that kind of presence– steady, dependable, bringing the comfort of God with you into every room you enter.

topics.title: Philemon and Onesimus
topics.summary: A runaway servant met Christ in Paul's prison cell, and everything changed. Paul sent Onesimus home carrying a letter that turns the world's categories upside down: receive him back, not as property, but as a beloved brother– and whatever he owes, put it on my account. This is the gospel in miniature. Jesus took our debt upon Himself and presented us to the Father as family. Forgive and receive one another the same way.

topics.title: Abigail
topics.summary: Abigail stepped into a moment of rising anger with wisdom and humility, and God used her to keep David from vengeance. One discerning word, offered at the right time, spared many lives and guarded a future king's heart. Her story teaches us that a gentle, courageous spirit can turn away wrath– and that God often places us in the path of conflict not to fuel it, but to make peace.

topics.title: Jael
topics.summary: God's victories rarely come the way we expect. When Sisera fled the battlefield, deliverance came not through an army but through Jael, a woman in a tent with ordinary tools in her hands. Scripture calls her blessed among women for her part in Israel's freedom, just as Deborah had foretold. The Lord can accomplish His purposes through anyone willing to act– and the honor of the victory always belongs to Him.

topics.title: The Widow of Zarephath
topics.summary: Down to her last bit of meal and a little oil, this widow chose to trust God's word over her own math. She fed the prophet first, and her supply never failed through the whole famine. When her son died, God raised him through Elijah, and her faith was made sure. Jesus himself pointed to her– a Gentile widow– as proof of how far His mercy reaches. Give God your little; He knows how to sustain you day by day.

topics.title: The Shunammite Woman
topics.summary: Hospitality opened this woman's home to the prophet, and God opened her womb in return. Yet the deeper lesson came when her promised son died. Pressed by grief, she could still say it was well, and she ran straight to God's prophet without letting go. Faith like hers doesn't deny the pain– it carries the pain directly to the only one who can raise the dead.

topics.title: Naaman
topics.summary: Naaman had rank, valor, and honor– and a disease none of it could cure. When the cure came, it offended him: no grand gesture, just a humble washing in the Jordan. Pride nearly sent him home a leper. But when he let go of how he thought God should work and simply obeyed, he came up clean and confessed the God of Israel. Healing often waits on the far side of humility.

topics.title: Gehazi
topics.summary: Gehazi watched grace given freely and decided to charge for it. He chased down Naaman's silver, lied to get it, then lied again to cover it– but nothing was hidden from his master, or from God. The leprosy Naaman left in the river became his own. A heart set on riches sinks into a snare of its own making. Guard yourself against covetousness before it costs you what silver can never buy back.

topics.title: Ruth and the Genealogy of Christ
topics.summary: Ruth was a Moabite outsider, yet God wrote her name into the family line of Jesus himself. Matthew's genealogy sets her alongside kings and patriarchs, a testimony that grace has always reached past borders and backgrounds. In God's perfect timing His Son came, born of a woman, through a lineage full of unlikely names. Your past does not disqualify you– He delights to graft the outsider into His redemption story.

topics.title: The Thief on the Cross
topics.summary: With hours left to live and nothing to offer, a dying thief turned to Jesus and asked only to be remembered. He had no baptism, no good deeds, no time to make anything right– and Jesus promised him paradise that very day. Salvation has always been a gift of grace received by faith, never something we earn. It is never too late to call on the Lord, and no past is too far gone for His mercy.

topics.title: The Prodigal Son
topics.summary: This parable is a portrait of the Father's heart. A son demanded his inheritance, wasted everything, and hit bottom in a pig pen before he came to his senses. He rehearsed a servant's speech on the road home, but his father was already running to meet him with a robe, a ring, and a feast. Heaven celebrates when the lost come home. If you've wandered, don't wait until you feel worthy– just get up and go. He's watching the road for you.

topics.title: The Good Samaritan
topics.summary: The religious men kept walking; mercy stopped. In this parable the ones expected to help would not be bothered, while a despised Samaritan bound wounds, carried the stranger to safety, and covered the cost. Jesus turns the question from who qualifies as my neighbor to whose neighbor I will be. Loving your neighbor as yourself is the royal law– and it's proven not in sentiment, but in what we're willing to stop and do.

topics.title: Simon of Cyrene
topics.summary: Simon was just passing through when soldiers pulled him from the crowd and laid the cross of Christ on his shoulders. What looked like an interruption became the moment history remembers him for. Jesus calls every follower to something similar: deny yourself, shoulder your cross daily, and walk behind Him. Often times God's greatest assignments arrive as inconveniences we didn't choose– glory in the cross anyway.

topics.title: The Parable of the Sower
topics.summary: The seed in this parable never changes– the soil does. God's word goes out and does not return empty, but what it produces depends on the heart receiving it. Hard paths lose it to the enemy, shallow soil wilts when trouble comes, and thorny hearts let worry and wealth choke it out. Good ground holds onto the word and bears fruit through patience. Ask the Lord to soften and clear your heart, so what He plants in you actually grows.

topics.title: The Wheat and the Tares
topics.summary: Wheat and weeds grow side by side in the same field, and for now that is how the kingdom looks in the world. Jesus taught that the enemy plants counterfeits among God's children, and the two won't be fully separated until the harvest at the close of the age. Judgment belongs to Christ and His angels, not to us. Our part is to grow as true wheat– rooted, fruitful, and patient– trusting God to sort the field in His time.

topics.title: The Mustard Seed
topics.summary: Don't despise small beginnings. The kingdom of God starts like a mustard seed– the smallest thing in the garden– and grows into something large enough to shelter the birds in its branches. What God plants may look insignificant at first, in your life or in your church, but His work carries growth inside it. Sow the small seed, stay faithful in the small day, and watch what He makes of it.

topics.title: The Hidden Treasure
topics.summary: Joy, not duty, moved the man in this parable to sell everything– he knew what the treasure was worth. Heaven's kingdom is that kind of find: once you truly see the value of knowing Christ, everything else grows small by comparison. Paul counted all his gains as loss for that same surpassing worth. Search for God the way you'd dig for hidden silver, and remember: wherever your treasure sits, your heart will follow.

topics.title: The Pearl of Great Price
topics.summary: The kingdom is worth everything you have. When the merchant found that one pearl, he gladly let everything else go — and Paul counted all his gains as loss next to knowing Christ. Here's the wonder: this treasure can't be bought with money, yet it costs you all you've been holding onto. Let go with joy. Nothing you surrender for Jesus compares to the worth of what you gain.

topics.title: The Lost Sheep
topics.summary: You are worth searching for. The shepherd doesn't shrug at one missing sheep out of a hundred — he goes out after it until he finds it, then carries it home rejoicing. Every one of us has wandered off to our own way, and God laid the weight of it all on Jesus so we could be brought back. If you've strayed, know this: heaven throws a celebration over a single sinner who turns around.

topics.title: The Lost Coin
topics.summary: Notice how hard the woman looks for one coin — lamp lit, house swept, searching every corner until it's found. That is the heart of Jesus toward the lost. He came into this world on a rescue mission for sinners, and the angels themselves rejoice when even one repents. You are not forgotten in some dusty corner; you are being sought. Let yourself be found.

topics.title: The Unforgiving Servant
topics.summary: We have been forgiven a debt we could never repay. That's where forgiveness starts — not with what someone owes you, but with the mountain God cancelled for you. The servant released from ten thousand talents then choked a man over pocket change, and his lord called the ugliness what it was. Hold your grievances up next to the cross. Mercy received must become mercy given, from the heart.

topics.title: The Laborers in the Vineyard
topics.summary: God's generosity doesn't follow our math. Whether you were called at daybreak or in the final hour, the reward flows from the goodness of the Master, not the length of your shift. It's tempting to compare — to feel the early worker's grumble rising in us — but salvation was never a wage. God shows mercy because He wills to show mercy. Be thankful He called you at all, and rejoice when latecomers receive the same kindness.

topics.title: The Two Sons
topics.summary: Talk is easy in the kingdom; obedience is the proof. One son refused his father outright, then thought better of it and went to work. The other gave all the right words and never showed up. Jesus asks which one honored the father's wishes — and the answer confronts us. Don't just call Him Lord. Be a doer of the word, because profession without practice is self-deception.

topics.title: The Wicked Husbandmen
topics.summary: God is patient, but His patience has a purpose — repentance, not presumption. The owner of the vineyard kept sending servants, and the tenants kept refusing them, until finally they killed his son. Yet man's worst rejection could not derail God's plan: the stone the builders tossed aside became the chief cornerstone. Receive the Son while He is offered. The vineyard belongs to those who bear its fruit for the Owner.

topics.title: The Wedding Feast
topics.summary: An invitation from the King is no small thing. Many who were first invited brushed the wedding aside, so the call went out to anyone who would come — and it still does. But notice the guest without a garment: entrance is on the King's terms, clothed in what He provides rather than our own righteousness. Answer the summons while the feast is set. Blessed are those who take their seat at the Lamb's table.

topics.title: The Ten Virgins
topics.summary: Readiness can't be borrowed. All ten virgins carried lamps, and all ten waited through the delay — the difference was oil. When the midnight cry came, the ready ones followed the bridegroom in, and the door closed behind the rest. Keep your lamp burning now... tend your own walk with Christ daily, because no one else's faith can cover you at His coming. You don't know the day or the hour. Stay awake in spirit and be found waiting.

topics.title: The Talents
topics.summary: What God has placed in your hands, He expects you to put to work. Each servant received according to his ability — the failure wasn't having one talent, it was burying it out of fear. The Master delights to say well done over faithfulness, and He entrusts more to those who steward the little. Don't let fear talk you into hiding what heaven gave you. Invest your gifts for the kingdom and let the increase testify.

topics.title: The Sheep and the Goats
topics.summary: One day the King will separate all people the way a shepherd divides his flock, and the evidence He points to is strikingly ordinary — food for the hungry, water for the thirsty, kindness toward the stranger, the sick, and the prisoner. Whatever we do for the least of His brothers and sisters, He counts as done to Him. Love for Jesus has hands and feet. Serve the overlooked around you; eternity itself takes notice.

topics.title: The Rich Fool
topics.summary: Full barns cannot secure a single tomorrow. The rich man in the parable had a growth plan for everything except his soul, and God called the whole enterprise foolish — that very night his life was required of him. Your life does not consist of what you own. Guard against covetousness, hold wealth loosely, and be rich toward God — generous in good works, storing up a foundation that death cannot touch.

topics.title: The Rich Man and Lazarus
topics.summary: Comfort in this life is no measure of standing with God. The rich man feasted while Lazarus lay hungry at his gate, but death reversed everything — and by then the gulf was fixed and could not be crossed. Notice too that no sign, not even someone returning from the dead, persuades a heart that ignores God's word. Take Scripture seriously now. Care for the sufferer at your gate now. Eternity settles what this life obscures.

topics.title: The Persistent Widow
topics.summary: Keep praying. Jesus told this parable for one reason — that we would pray always and not lose heart. If even a judge with no fear of God finally answered a widow who wouldn't quit, how much more will our Father answer His children who cry out to Him day and night? Delay is not denial. So bring the request again. Persistence in prayer is itself an act of faith — and faith is what Jesus will be looking for when He returns.

topics.title: The Pharisee and the Publican
topics.summary: Self-congratulation is not prayer. The Pharisee stood recounting his virtues; the tax collector stood far off, unable even to lift his eyes, pleading only for mercy as a sinner — and he was the one who went home justified. God resists the proud but pours grace on the humble, looking with favor on the contrite heart that trembles at His word. Come to Him honest about your need. That is the prayer heaven hears.

topics.title: The Two Debtors
topics.summary: When a debt too large to repay is simply wiped away, the heart cannot help but overflow with love. The woman who wept at Jesus' feet grasped how much she had been pardoned, and it poured out in worship. The one who feels little forgiven loves little in return. Paul called himself the worst of sinners, yet found grace running over — and so may we. The more clearly we see what Christ has cancelled, the more freely we love.

topics.title: The Great Supper
topics.summary: The table is set, the feast is ready, and the call goes out — yet how often we answer with excuses. Those first invited turned away for their fields and business, so the master flung his doors open to the poor, the broken, the overlooked. Heaven's welcome still stands. The Spirit calls and the bride echoes it: come. Whoever thirsts may drink freely from the well of life. Don't let lesser things keep you from the greatest feast.

topics.title: Building the Tower
topics.summary: Before a builder raises a tower, he sits down and counts the cost. Before a king marches to war, he weighs whether he can win. Jesus asks the same of us — following Him is no small thing. It means loosening our grip on all we hold, keeping our hand steady on the plow without glancing back. He warned one eager scribe that He Himself had no place to rest His head. Count the cost, yes — then follow anyway, for He is worth it all.

topics.title: Water into Wine
topics.summary: At a wedding in Cana, the wine ran dry — and Jesus quietly turned plain water into the finest the feast had tasted. It was His first sign, the first unveiling of His glory, and His disciples came to believe in Him. Notice how the best was saved for last. God's timing so often works this way... the joy He pours out surpasses anything we could arrange for ourselves. Wine gladdens the heart, and richer still is the gladness Christ brings to those who trust Him.

topics.title: Feeding the Five Thousand
topics.summary: A boy's small meal — five loaves and a couple of fish — seemed nothing against a hungry multitude. Yet Jesus took the little that was offered, lifted His eyes to heaven, gave thanks, and broke it. Thousands ate their fill, and twelve baskets of fragments were gathered up after. This is how our God works. He does not despise small beginnings; He blesses what we place in His hands and makes it more than enough. Bring Him your little, and watch what He can multiply.

topics.title: Walking on the Water
topics.summary: In the darkest hour of the night, Jesus came to His frightened disciples, walking upon the waves. Peter dared to step out and, for a moment, walked toward Him — until he saw the wind and began to sink. But the Lord's hand was quick to catch him. How like us, to falter when we stare at the storm instead of the Savior. Fear whispers that we're going under; faith fixes our eyes on Him. Be not afraid, He still says. It is I.

topics.title: Calming the Storm
topics.summary: The waves crashed over the boat while Jesus slept, and His terrified disciples woke Him certain they would drown. He rose, spoke a word to wind and wave, and a great calm fell. Then He asked them why they were so afraid, where their faith had gone. Even wind and waves know His voice and obey. Whatever storm is breaking over your life, remember who is in the boat with you — the One who stills the raging sea can quiet your heart.

topics.title: Healing the Blind
topics.summary: The disciples saw a man blind from birth and asked whose sin had caused it. Jesus answered that it was no one's fault — this was a canvas for God's works to shine. He made clay, sent the man to wash, and sight came flooding in. The healed man couldn't argue theology, but he knew one thing: once he was blind, and now he could see. That is the testimony of everyone Christ touches. He still opens eyes, both the body's and the soul's.

topics.title: Healing the Leper
topics.summary: Under the law, a leper lived as an outcast — clothing torn, forced to cry out his own uncleanness, cut off from every human touch. Then one such man knelt before Jesus, believing that if the Lord was willing, He could make him clean. And Jesus, moved with compassion, did the unthinkable — He reached out and touched him. I am willing, He said. Be clean. No one is too defiled or too far gone for His healing hand. Come as you are, and let Him make you whole.

topics.title: Healing the Paralytic
topics.summary: Four friends were so determined to bring their paralyzed companion to Jesus that they tore open a roof to lower him down. Jesus saw their faith — and His first words spoke not to the man's legs but to his soul: your sins are forgiven. Then, to prove He held that authority, He told him to rise, gather his mat, and walk home. And he did. Our deepest need is always mercy for the heart. The One who heals the body has power to pardon the soul.

topics.title: Raising Jairus' Daughter
topics.summary: A synagogue ruler named Jairus fell at Jesus' feet, begging Him to heal his dying girl. Before they arrived, word came that she had died — why trouble the Teacher now? But Jesus was unshaken. To Him, her death was only sleep. He took her cold hand and spoke: little one, arise. Her spirit returned; she stood and walked. Death itself yields to His voice. When grief says it is over, He calls us still to set fear aside and simply believe.

topics.title: The Woman with the Issue of Blood
topics.summary: For twelve long years a woman bled, spending all she had on physicians who only left her worse. Desperate, she pressed through the crowd with a single thought — if she could just brush the hem of His garment, she would be healed. And she was, the instant her fingers touched the cloth. Jesus felt it and turned, not to scold her but to bless her: daughter, your faith has healed you, go now in peace. Bring Him even your trembling, worn-out faith. It is enough.

topics.title: The Ten Lepers
topics.summary: Ten lepers cried out for mercy, and Jesus healed them all as they went. Yet only one — a Samaritan, an outsider — turned back to fall at His feet in thanks. Where, Jesus asked, were the other nine? All ten were cleansed, but just one returned to give God the glory. How easily we do the same, taking blessing after blessing and forgetting the Giver. Call your soul to bless Him, and never forget all His benefits. A grateful heart is the one made truly whole.

topics.title: The Centurion's Servant
topics.summary: A Roman centurion came to Jesus for his suffering servant, then stopped Him before He reached the house. He did not need Jesus under his roof — a single word would do. As a soldier, he understood authority: he spoke, and men obeyed. He trusted that Christ's word carried the same power over sickness. Jesus marveled at such faith, and the servant was healed that very hour. God sends His word and it accomplishes His will. Do we trust His word like that?

topics.title: The Widow of Nain's Son
topics.summary: A widow followed her only son toward the grave, her last hope carried out before her. No one asked Jesus to step in — He simply saw her, and His heart broke with compassion. Weep not, He told her, and laid His hand on the bier. Then He spoke life into the dead: young man, arise. The boy sat up, and Jesus gave him back to his mother. Long before, Elijah had watched God do the very same. Our Lord still draws near to the grieving; His compassion moves Him to act.

topics.title: The Draught of Fishes
topics.summary: All night Peter labored and drew up nothing. Then at a word from the Lord, he let the net down once more– and it strained under the weight of the catch. What our own strength cannot manage, obedience to Christ can fill to overflowing. He still calls ordinary hands to gather souls, and where he sends us, the net will not break.

topics.title: The Withered Hand
topics.summary: They watched to see whether he would dare a healing on the sabbath, more concerned with the rule than with the man suffering in front of them. But mercy does not wait for a convenient day. Jesus grieved over hearts so hard they would loose an ox from the stall yet begrudge a man his healing. He called him to stretch out the very hand that could not move, and in the reaching it was made whole. Doing good is never out of season.

topics.title: The Man at the Pool
topics.summary: Thirty-eight years he lay by that water, always too slow, always without anyone to help him in. Jesus came and asked the searching question: did he truly want to be well? Wholeness did not rise from the troubled pool but from the voice of Christ, calling him to stand and walk. The Lord still strengthens us on our bed of weakness and seeks us out where we lie. He asks us the same today, and bids us leave our sin behind.

topics.title: The Deaf and Dumb Man
topics.summary: The Lord who fashioned every mouth and ear took a struggling man aside from the crowd and touched him with his own hands. What the prophets had promised came to pass: ears unstopped, a tongue set free to speak plainly. He does not heal from a distance or in a hurry. He draws near to the broken and works with tender care. Whatever is bound up in you, he is able to open. Everything he does, he does well.

topics.title: The Coin in the Fish
topics.summary: Faced with a tax he had no money to pay, the Lord sent Peter to the sea to draw up a fish with a coin waiting in its mouth. The One who owns the cattle on a thousand hills is never at a loss for ways to meet our need. We are not called to anxious scheming but to seek his kingdom first and leave the rest to him. Whatever you lack today, your Father already knows... and his supply is as near as his word.

topics.title: The Barren Fig Tree
topics.summary: The owner came looking for fruit and found only leaves, season after season. Justice was ready to cut the tree down, but mercy asked for one more year to dig around it and feed its roots. Such is the patience of God with us– he grants time, and he lends his care, but he is still looking for fruit. A faith that shows leaves and nothing more will not satisfy him. Let this be the year you bear something real for him.

topics.title: The Good Shepherd Parable
topics.summary: A good shepherd knows his sheep by name, and they know the sound of his voice. Jesus is that shepherd for us, not a hired hand but the One who laid down his very life for the flock. Those who belong to him hear him and follow, and he holds them so securely that no one can snatch them from his hand. We did not shape ourselves; we are his own, sheep he tends and keeps. Listen for his voice today, and go where he leads.

topics.title: New Wine, New Bottles
topics.summary: You cannot pour the new life of the kingdom into the old vessel of a former self– the old will simply burst. Christ does not come to patch us up; he makes us new creatures altogether, the old things passing away. God is forever doing a new thing, opening a road through what looked like wilderness. Do not cling to what he stands ready to replace. Let him hand you a heart made fresh to hold all that he is pouring out.

topics.title: The House on the Rock
topics.summary: Two men built, and from the outside their houses may have looked the same. But when the rains came and the floods rose, only one stood: the house dug deep and founded on rock. It is not enough to hear the words of Christ; the wise man puts them into practice. Storms visit every life, and what you have built upon will be laid bare. Set your feet on the one foundation that cannot be moved, Christ himself, and you will stand.

topics.title: Signs and Wonders of the Apostles
topics.summary: The apostles had no silver or gold to offer, but they carried the name of Jesus, and in that name a lame man rose and walked. Through their hands God poured out signs and wonders. Shadows that brought healing, cloths that carried his power, the sick made well. None of it sprang from their own strength. God himself was bearing witness to the gospel they preached. The same Lord still confirms his word wherever people go out in his name.

topics.title: Peter Raised Dorcas
topics.summary: Dorcas was known for her kindness, a woman whose hands clothed the widows and whose days overflowed with good works. When she died, her friends stood weeping over the garments she had sewn. Peter knelt to pray, and at his word to arise, her eyes opened and she looked up. The God who summons the dead to life gave her back to them, and many came to believe. A quiet life of love is never wasted, and the God who raised Lazarus still holds power over the grave.

topics.title: The Body of Christ
topics.summary: The body is a single whole, and yet it is made of many parts, and not one of them is spare. By one Spirit we were formed into a single body, and no member can say to another that it has no need of him. Christ is the head, and from him the whole frame grows together, knit and supplied in love. You were never meant to walk with him alone. You belong to the body, set in your place on purpose and needed by the rest.

topics.title: Members One of Another
topics.summary: We are not merely individuals who happen to gather in the same room; in Christ we are joined as members of one another. When one part suffers, the whole body aches with it, and when one is honored, the rest rejoice. So we weep alongside those who mourn and shoulder the burdens too heavy to carry alone. The weakest among us are not the least but the most needed. Care for the one who suffers as if it were your own body, because it is.

topics.title: The Household of Faith
topics.summary: In Christ you are no longer an outsider or a stranger, but family– a fellow citizen with all the saints, a member of God's own household. Together we are being built into a holy temple, living stones raised upon the cornerstone that is Christ himself. The church is where the living God dwells, the pillar and support of the truth. So let us do good to everyone, and most of all to those who share this household of faith. You were brought near to belong.

topics.title: Not Forsaking the Assembly
topics.summary: Faith was never designed to be carried alone. The first believers met daily, shared meals in one another's homes, and did it with glad and simple hearts, staying up late together just to hear the word. Show up for each other. Your presence stirs up love and good works in someone who needs it, and theirs does the same for you. God leans in when his people speak of him, and heaven keeps a record of those conversations. Don't drift from the gathering. Keep at it, all the more as the Day draws near.

topics.title: One Body, Many Gifts
topics.summary: One Spirit hands out many gifts, and not one of them is meant to sit idle. Wisdom, knowledge, faith, healing, teaching, service — each is a different working of the same God, given not to elevate you but to build up the body around you. Whatever grace you've received, you are a steward of it. Put it to work for the good of the whole, and the whole body grows into all Christ intended it to be.

topics.title: Church Leadership
topics.summary: Leading God's people is a good work, but it asks much of the one who takes it up. Scripture sets a high bar: blameless, self-controlled, hospitable, quick to teach and slow to anger, never chasing money or lording over those in his care. A true leader tends the flock willingly and leads by example, remembering the church was purchased at the highest price. Those who serve well are worthy of honor.

topics.title: Deacons
topics.summary: When the first church grew, the apostles saw that the work of prayer and the Word could not be set aside to wait on tables, so servants were chosen to carry that load. Deacons are marked by honest reputation, sober living, and a faith held in a clear conscience. Think of Stephen, full of the Spirit, or Phebe, who served her church faithfully. Those who serve well earn a good standing and grow bold in the faith.

topics.title: Shepherding the Flock
topics.summary: To shepherd God's people is to feed them, not yourself. Jesus pressed it into Peter three times: if you love me, care for my sheep. The Spirit sets overseers to watch over a flock purchased at the cost of blood, and God promises pastors after His own heart who nourish with wisdom and understanding. But Scripture warns hard against shepherds who fatten themselves while the sheep go hungry. Tend them well. They are His, not yours.

topics.title: Church Discipline
topics.summary: Correction in the church is never about winning. It's about winning back. Scripture lays out a patient path: go first to your brother alone, then with one or two others, then before the body, always aiming to restore him gently and watching your own heart lest you fall the same way. The goal is never to crush but to rescue, and when he turns, forgiveness and comfort must follow quickly. We warn as family, never as enemies.

topics.title: Unity in the Church
topics.summary: Unity isn't sameness — it's oneness held together in peace. We're bound as one body under one Lord, sharing one faith, one hope, one calling from one God who is Father of us all. Jesus Himself prayed we would be one, just as He and the Father are one, so the watching world would believe. What a good and pleasant thing it is when brothers dwell without division, knit together in heart and mind. Guard that bond well.

topics.title: Elders and Overseers
topics.summary: Those who lead the church carry a weight few see; they keep watch over your souls and will answer to God for how they do it. Scripture asks us to honor them, to obey their godly leadership, and to hold them in high esteem for the labor they pour out. Elders who lead well deserve double honor; they teach, they guard sound doctrine, and they pray over the sick, anointing them in the Lord's name. Make their work a joy, not a grief.

topics.title: The Lord's Supper
topics.summary: On the night He was betrayed, Jesus took bread and a cup and gave them a meaning that would outlast the ages: the bread His body, the cup His blood, broken and poured out for you. Every time we come to His table, we remember that surrender and proclaim His death until He returns. The cup we bless and the bread we break join us to Christ and to one another, many as we are, made one. Come, but come examined — this is holy ground, not habit.

topics.title: Baptism into Christ
topics.summary: Baptism is no empty ritual. It's a burial and a rising. Going down into the water, we are joined to the death of Christ; coming up, we are raised with Him into a wholly new life. Scripture ties it to repentance and the washing away of sin, the Spirit given as a gift, and a heart that truly believes, like the eunuch who asked what could keep him from the water. Go under as one who has died. Rise as one made new in Him.

topics.title: The Church as a Temple
topics.summary: You belong to God, not to yourself. You are a dwelling place for His Spirit. Scripture calls the gathered believers a temple, each of us a living stone framed together into a holy house where God Himself makes His home. It is a staggering thing that the Lord of heaven would live in and walk among His people. So we keep the temple pure, offering our lives as spiritual sacrifices. What is holy was never meant to share room with idols.

topics.title: The Bride of Christ
topics.summary: The church is not merely a crowd or an institution. She is a bride, loved by Christ with a love that gave everything for her. He gave Himself to make her holy, cleansing her by His word and presenting her radiant, without spot. One day the wedding of the Lamb will come, and she will stand arrayed in white, ready for her Bridegroom. Let this settle deep: as a groom delights over his bride, so your God rejoices over you.

topics.title: The First Church
topics.summary: The first believers were a family, not a program. They gave themselves to the apostles' teaching, to prayer, to breaking bread in one another's homes, and to each other. No one clung to what he owned; they shared so no one among them went without. Day by day they met with glad and simple hearts, praising God as the Lord kept adding to their number. This is what life in the Spirit looks like: worship, open hands... and Jesus on every tongue that would not fall silent.

topics.title: Sharing All Things
topics.summary: The early church held their possessions loosely because they held one another dearly. Knit together in heart, no one counted his goods as his alone; those who had, sold and shared so that not a single person went in need. It's a picture of holy equality: your abundance meeting another's lack today, theirs meeting yours tomorrow. And John presses the question home: if you have plenty and shut your heart to a brother in need, how does God's love truly live in you?

topics.title: Ordaining Elders
topics.summary: Raising up leaders was never done lightly in Scripture. Paul and Barnabas appointed elders in each young church only after prayer and fasting, entrusting them to God's care. When Barnabas and Saul were set apart, it came at the Spirit's word, sealed with fasting and hands laid on in prayer. And Timothy was warned not to rush it: don't lay hands hastily, and don't neglect the gift stirred up in you. Calling is holy work. Handle it with care and clean hands.

topics.title: The Jerusalem Council
topics.summary: A dispute threatened to divide the young church, and its apostles and elders refused to act alone or in haste. They gathered to weigh the matter together. What they decided bore a humble stamp: the Spirit had led them, and they would lay no needless burden on the Gentiles. Then they sent trusted men to deliver the ruling in person. Here is the wisdom of it: where there is no counsel a people falls, but safety comes through many wise counselors.

topics.title: Gathering in Homes
topics.summary: The early church didn't need grand buildings. It gathered around kitchen tables and in living rooms, where believers greeted one another, broke bread, and prayed together under ordinary roofs, and the apostles carried their teaching from one household to the next. Wherever God's people gather in His name, that place becomes holy ground. Open your home, and watch how He fills it.

topics.title: Serving in the Church
topics.summary: Every one of us has been handed a gift, not to hoard but to pour out for the good of others. Scripture calls us to serve one another in love, fervent in spirit, laboring as those who serve the Lord Himself. And take heart: God is not forgetful. The quiet work of love you show toward His people, done in His name, He remembers and will reward.

topics.title: Honoring Faithful Leaders
topics.summary: God sets faithful shepherds over us for our good, those who labor in the word, who guide and correct us in love. Scripture urges us to know them, to esteem them highly, and to count those who lead well as deserving of double honor. Remember their walk. Follow their faith. What's asked of every steward is simply this: that he be found faithful.

topics.title: Bearing One Another's Burdens
topics.summary: None of us was made to carry the weight alone. When a brother stumbles under a load too heavy, we come alongside and lift — the strong steadying the weak, the whole body holding up its own. Two really are better than one; where one falls, the other reaches down to raise him. Bear each other's burdens this way, and you fulfill the very law of Christ.

topics.title: Speaking the Truth in Love
topics.summary: Truth and love were never meant to be separated. Spoken together, they become the very thing that grows us up into Christ, who is the Head, while the whole body is knit and fitted together, each part supplying the rest. Honesty without tenderness wounds; tenderness without honesty flatters. As iron sharpens iron, we sharpen one another, always for building up and never for tearing down.

topics.title: The Church Militant
topics.summary: Christ Himself promised to build His church, and He declared that the powers of hell will never overcome it. Think of it — empires have risen to crush God's people, yet what is truly of God can never be overthrown. No weapon shaped against you will win. This victory doesn't come by our might or our power, but by His Spirit. And if God is for us, who could possibly stand against us?

topics.title: Bishops and Their Qualities
topics.summary: What qualifies a spiritual leader isn't talent or ambition — it's character. Scripture asks that an overseer be blameless and self-controlled, gentle rather than quarrelsome, hospitable, sober, and able to teach; not a lover of money, not a new convert puffed up with pride. He must lead not as a lord over God's flock, but as an example the flock can safely follow. Who a man is matters far more than what he can do.

topics.title: The Priesthood of Believers
topics.summary: Under the old covenant only a priest could draw near — but no longer. Because Christ has cleansed us by His own blood, He has made every believer a priest and a king before God. You are living stones built into a spiritual house, a chosen and royal priesthood, called to offer up the sacrifices of worship and a surrendered life. The veil is torn. Draw near now, with boldness, straight into the holiest place.

topics.title: Spiritual Growth Together
topics.summary: We were never meant to grow up in isolation. Maturity comes as a body. Together we press toward true unity in the faith, toward the full stature and measure of Christ Himself. No longer are we children, tossed about by every clever teaching that blows through. Instead we mature in His grace, coming to know our Lord more deeply, each one built up so the whole church is strengthened. Press on. You're growing, and you're not growing alone.

topics.title: Care for the Widows
topics.summary: From the beginning, God has kept a tender watch over the widow, and He asks His people to do the same. Pure and undefiled religion, James tells us, looks like this: visiting the fatherless and the widowed in their distress. When the early church saw its widows overlooked, it moved quickly to see them cared for. Think of Dorcas, whose hands stitched clothing for the needy until the whole room wept at her passing. Honor them. Provide for them. This is the very heart of God.

topics.title: Collections for the Saints
topics.summary: Generosity has always marked God's people. When fellow believers in Jerusalem fell into poverty, the churches gathered a collection, each one setting something aside and giving as the Lord had prospered him. And here is the wonder of it: the Macedonians, though crushed by their own affliction and deep poverty, begged for the privilege of giving. Set your gift aside willingly, according to what you have. God weighs the heart behind the hand.

topics.title: Fellowship of Believers
topics.summary: Fellowship is far more than friendly company. It's shared life with the Father and His Son, and so with one another. When we live openly in His light, our hearts are knit together and the blood of Christ keeps cleansing us. The first believers gave themselves to this: to teaching, to breaking bread, to prayer. Even those who simply feared the Lord and spoke of Him together were noticed by heaven, their names written in His book of remembrance.

topics.title: The Church's Mission
topics.summary: We are not lit up to be hidden. Christ calls His church the world's light, a city on a hill that cannot be concealed, a lamp set high to fill the whole house. So let your light shine before others. Filled with His Spirit, we are sent as witnesses to the very ends of the earth, holding out the word that brings life to a crooked generation. Go, then. Make disciples of every nation, and know that He is with you always.

topics.title: Confessing Faults to One Another
topics.summary: Hidden sin festers in the dark, but confession brings it into the light where healing begins. Scripture urges us to open our faults to one another and to pray, so that we may be made whole. When we admit our sins, God is ever faithful and just; He forgives and cleanses every one. Cover your sin and you'll never prosper; confess it and forsake it, and mercy will meet you. When someone stumbles, restore him gently, in a spirit of meekness.

topics.title: The Pillar of Truth
topics.summary: The church stands as the pillar and support of the truth, God's own living house, set to hold His word high for all to see. That is a sacred trust. We're called to guard the sound teaching handed to us, keeping it by the Holy Spirit who lives within, and to contend earnestly for the faith once delivered to the saints. Hold fast. Take heed to yourself and to what you teach, for in doing so you safeguard both your own soul and those who hear you.

topics.title: Restoring the Fallen
topics.summary: When a brother or sister stumbles, we aren't called to condemn but to gently lift them back. Restore the fallen with a humble spirit, watching your own footing all the while. Forgive the one weighed down by sorrow, and comfort him before grief swallows him whole. To turn a wanderer back from error is to draw a soul back from death itself and cover a heap of sin. And often times it's the very ones the enemy has sifted like wheat who, once restored, turn and strengthen the rest of us.

topics.title: Growing the Church
topics.summary: One plants, another waters, but the increase belongs to God alone. We're only laborers in His field, coworkers on a building He is raising. Our part is faithful work; the growth is always His to give. As the whole body stays joined to Christ its Head, knit together joint by joint, it rises like a living temple— grounded in faith and multiplying day by day. Plant where you're placed, and trust the Lord to bring the harvest.

topics.title: Assembling with Joy
topics.summary: There's a gladness that rises in us when we're called to God's house. The psalmist's soul ached for the courts of the Lord— one thing he desired above all: to dwell there and behold His beauty. We were never meant to walk this road alone. So don't drift from the gathering; the early believers met day by day, breaking bread with glad and open hearts, praising God together. Come with joy. His presence is worth the meeting.

topics.title: The Family of God
topics.summary: God is Father over one great family, named in heaven and on earth. In Christ, kinship runs deeper than blood— whoever does what God wills is your brother, your sister, your mother. So honor the older among you as parents and the younger as your own, with all purity. Do good to everyone, and especially to those within the family of faith. Our God takes the solitary and sets them in a home. You belong here.

topics.title: Overcoming Fear
topics.summary: The moment we remember who stands beside us, fear begins to lose its grip. God has not handed you a spirit of fear, but one of power, love, and a sound mind. When dread creeps in, meet it with trust— what can mere flesh do to the one God upholds? His perfect love drives the torment out. So be strong and take courage; you do not face tomorrow alone. The Lord your God goes with you wherever the road leads.

topics.title: Finding Peace
topics.summary: The peace Christ gives is nothing like the world's fragile calm. When worry rises, He invites you to trade it— bring every anxious request to God in prayer, wrapped in thanksgiving, and a peace beyond understanding will stand guard over your heart and mind. Keep your thoughts fixed on Him and He keeps you in perfect peace. Let that peace rule within you. Then you can lie down and sleep, knowing the Lord alone keeps you safe.

topics.title: Real Joy
topics.summary: Real joy isn't manufactured; it's found in God's presence, where gladness is full and pleasures never end. This joy runs deeper than circumstance. Even when the fig tree fails to bloom and the fields yield nothing, the faithful heart still rejoices in its God. Christ spoke His words so that His own joy would live in us and overflow. Let the God of hope fill you— for delight in the Lord becomes your strength.

topics.title: Dealing with Anger
topics.summary: Not all anger is sin— but left unchecked, it hands ground to the enemy. Don't let the sun set on your wrath. Be quick to listen, slow to speak, and slower still to boil over— the one who masters his own spirit is stronger than the warrior who takes a city. A gentle answer can cool a rising temper, while harsh words only feed the fire. Guard your spirit, for resentment makes its home in the heart of a fool.

topics.title: Battling Depression
topics.summary: When the soul sinks low and everything within feels disquieted, it's alright to ask why— and then to turn that ache toward hope in God. Even Elijah, worn to the point of begging to die, was met not with rebuke but with rest, food, and strength for the road ahead. The Lord stays near the downcast; He can lift you out of the miry pit, set your feet on solid rock, and put a fresh song of praise on your lips. His mercies are new every morning; great is His faithfulness. Take heart— morning is coming.

topics.title: Overcoming Discouragement
topics.summary: Discouragement tells you to quit; God tells you to keep going. When your hands hang limp and your knees feel weak, He calls you to lift them up and steady your path. Don't grow weary in doing good— there's a harvest waiting in due season for the one who won't give up. Stand firm and let your heart be strengthened, for the Lord walks with you and holds your steps. Wait on Him. He will renew the strength within you, and you'll yet see His goodness among the living.

topics.title: Guarding Your Heart
topics.summary: Guard your heart above everything else, for the whole course of your life flows out of it. What takes root within eventually shows itself— from the heart come our words and deeds, both the beautiful and the ugly. And the heart is a slippery thing, deceptive beyond our own reading of it; only the Lord truly searches it. So ask Him to create in you a clean heart and a right spirit. Then feed your mind on whatever is true, pure, lovely, and worthy of praise.

topics.title: A Broken Heart
topics.summary: A heart in pieces doesn't drive God away— it draws Him near. He is especially close to the brokenhearted and saves those crushed low in spirit. Strange as it sounds, a broken and contrite heart is the very offering He treasures; He will never turn it away.
